docs.title: Welcome to the AD4x4 API
docs.text: This documentation provides a comprehensive overview of the AD4x4 API, covering everything you need to know to get started. The API is designed to be easy to use and follows standard REST conventions.

docs.title: Main Resources
docs.text:
The AD4x4 API is organized around a few main resources:

  • Authentication and Profiles: Manage user accounts, profiles, and authentication.
  • Members: Manage member profiles and information.
  • Vehicles: Register and manage member vehicles.
  • Trips: Create, manage, and view off-road trips. Includes trip search and lead trip history.
  • Meeting Points: Define and manage meeting points for trips.
  • Upgrade Requests: Handle requests for user account upgrades.
  • Logbook Migration: Migrate from paper logbook to digital.
  • Account Deletion: Manage the account deletion process.
  • Notifications: Configure and manage user notifications.
  • UI Strings: Retrieve and manage editable UI strings for the client applications.
  • Permissions System: Control user access to different parts of the API.

docs.title: Account Deletion
docs.text: This document explains how a user can request, view, and cancel the deletion of their account.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
The account deletion process is designed to be simple and secure. It involves these main steps:

  1. The user makes an API request to signal their intent to delete their account.
  2. A 3-day grace period begins, during which the user can cancel the request.
  3. After the grace period, a background process anonymizes the user's data.

This grace period allows for a "cooling off" period, during which the user can change their mind. The anonymization process ensures that all personally identifiable information is removed from the user's profile, while preserving the integrity of any content they may have created (e.g., trip comments).

docs.title: Request Account Deletion
docs.text:
Initiate the account deletion process.

POST /api/members/request-deletion

Note: This endpoint does NOT use a trailing slash and does not require any request body.

Authentication: Required (Bearer token)

The authenticated user associated with the request will be marked for deletion.

Success Response (200 OK):

{
    "success": true,
    "message": "deletion_request_submitted"
}

Error Response (400 Bad Request - Already pending):

{
    "success": false,
    "message": "deletion_request_already_exists"
}

docs.title: View Deletion Request
docs.text:
Check the status of an existing deletion request.

GET /api/members/deletion-request

Note: This endpoint does NOT use a trailing slash.

Authentication: Required (Bearer token)

Success Response (200 OK):

{
    "success": true,
    "message": {
        "id": 1,
        "member": 123,
        "requestedAt": "2026-03-15T10:00:00"
    }
}

Error Response (404 Not Found):

{
    "success": false,
    "message": "deletion_request_not_found"
}

docs.title: Cancel Account Deletion
docs.text:
Cancel a pending deletion request before the 3-day grace period expires.

POST /api/members/cancel-deletion

Note: This endpoint does NOT use a trailing slash and does not require any request body.

Authentication: Required (Bearer token)

Success Response (200 OK):

{
    "success": true,
    "message": "deletion_request_cancelled"
}

Error Response (404 Not Found):

{
    "success": false,
    "message": "deletion_request_not_found"
}

docs.title: Anonymization Details
docs.text:
After the 3-day grace period, the user's account will be anonymized. This is a permanent and irreversible action. The following fields will be changed:

  • The user will be marked as inactive.
  • The username will be replaced with a randomly generated string (e.g., deleted_user_...).
  • The email address will be changed to a dummy address (e.g., ...@deleted.com).
  • The first name will be set to "Anonymous".
  • The last name will be cleared.

docs.text: • Background Tasks - The process_account_deletion_requests task runs daily at midnight.

docs.title: API Concepts
docs.text: This document covers high-level concepts for interacting with the AD4x4 API.

docs.title: Time Zone
docs.text:
All dates and times in the API use Asia/Dubai time zone (UTC+4) with no daylight saving time.

Examples: - 2026-03-15T07:00:00+04:00 - March 15, 2026 at 7:00 AM Dubai time - 2026-03-14T18:00:00+04:00 - March 14, 2026 at 6:00 PM Dubai time

Important: The USE_TZ setting is False, so times are stored and returned as-is in Dubai time without UTC conversion.

docs.title: Authentication
docs.text:
The API uses JWT (JSON Web Token) authentication. To authenticate:

  1. Obtain Token: POST to /api/token/ with username and password
  2. Use Token: Include in Authorization header as Bearer <token>
  3. Refresh Token: POST to /api/token/refresh/ with refresh token

docs.title: Authentication Header Format
docs.text: Authorization: Bearer <your_jwt_token>

docs.title: Obtain Token Pair
docs.text:
• Endpoint: POST /api/token/
  • Body: json { "username": "your_username", "password": "your_password" }
  • Response: json { "access": "eyJ0eXAiOiJKV1QiLCJhbGc...", "refresh": "eyJ0eXAiOiJKV1QiLCJhbGc..." }

docs.title: Refresh Token
docs.text:
• Endpoint: POST /api/token/refresh/
  • Body: json { "refresh": "eyJ0eXAiOiJKV1QiLCJhbGc..." }
  • Response: json { "access": "eyJ0eXAiOiJKV1QiLCJhbGc..." }

docs.title: Token Expiration
docs.text: JWT access tokens expire after 1 day (24 hours). When a token expires, you will receive a 401 Unauthorized response. Use the refresh token endpoint to obtain a new access token.

docs.title: Authentication Error Responses
docs.text:
The API returns standard HTTP status codes for authentication errors:

Status Detail Message Meaning 401 Expired JWT. Token has expired. Obtain a new token via refresh. 401 User account is disabled. User account has been deactivated. 401 Token has been invalidated. Password was changed, or token was revoked. Re-authenticate. 401 Invalid JWT payload. Token is malformed or tampered with. 401 User not found. User associated with token no longer exists.

docs.title: Cross-Origin Requests (CORS)
docs.text:
The API supports Cross-Origin Resource Sharing (CORS) for specific allowed origins:

Origin Description http://localhost Local development http://127.0.0.1 Local development https://ap.ad4x4.com Production web app https://*.sandbox.novita.ai Sandbox environments (regex match)

Note: CORS is configured via an explicit whitelist (CORS_ORIGIN_WHITELIST) and a regex pattern for sandbox URLs. CORS_ORIGIN_ALLOW_ALL is not enabled. Requests from other origins will be rejected. If you need to access the API from a new origin, contact the administrators.

docs.title: Response Format
docs.text: Most endpoints return responses in the following formats. Note that the message field can be either a string or an object depending on the endpoint.

docs.title: Success Response (Unified)
docs.text:
When message is a string:

{
  "success": true,
  "message": "operation_successful"
}

When message is an object (data responses):

{
  "success": true,
  "message": {
    "id": 456,
    "title": "Weekend Trip",
    ...
  }
}

docs.title: Error Response (Unified)
docs.text:
When message is a string:

{
  "success": false,
  "message": "error_description"
}

When message is an object (validation errors):

{
  "success": false,
  "message": {
    "field_name": [
      "This field is required."
    ]
  }
}

docs.title: List Response (Paginated)
docs.text:
{
  "count": 100,
  "next": "http://api.example.org/api/items/?page=3",
  "previous": "http://api.example.org/api/items/?page=1",
  "results": []
}

docs.title: Error Handling
docs.text: The API uses standard HTTP status codes and returns detailed error messages.

docs.title: 400 Bad Request
docs.text:
{
  "success": false,
  "message": {
    "field_name": [
      "This field is required."
    ],
    "another_field": [
      "Invalid value."
    ]
  }
}

docs.title: 401 Unauthorized
docs.text:
{
  "detail": "Authentication credentials were not provided."
}

or

{
  "detail": "Given token not valid for any token type"
}

docs.title: 403 Forbidden
docs.text:
{
  "success": false,
  "message": "no_permission_to_perform_action"
}

docs.title: 404 Not Found
docs.text:
{
  "detail": "Not found."
}

docs.title: 422 Unprocessable Entity
docs.text:
{
  "success": false,
  "message": "waitlist_enforced_globally"
}

docs.title: 500 Internal Server Error
docs.text:
{
  "error": "An unexpected error occurred. Please try again later."
}

docs.title: Trailing Slash Convention
docs.text:
Some endpoints use a trailing slash and others do not. This depends on how the endpoint is registered in the URL configuration.

General Rule: - Router-registered endpoints (ViewSets) use trailing slashes: /api/trips/, /api/members/, /api/vehicles/ - Manually registered endpoints (explicit URL paths) typically do NOT use trailing slashes: /api/members/search, /api/trips/456/register, /api/members/123/triphistory

Note: Using the wrong convention will result in a redirect or 404 error. Check the specific endpoint documentation for the correct format.

docs.title: File Uploads
docs.text: Endpoints that accept file uploads (images, track files, etc.) use multipart/form-data encoding.

docs.title: Example: Upload Trip Image
docs.text:
curl -X PATCH http://localhost:8000/api/trips/456/ \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_JWT_TOKEN" \
  -F "image=@/path/to/image.jpg" \
  -F "title=Updated Trip Title"

docs.title: Supported File Types
docs.text:
• Images: JPEG, PNG, GIF
  • Track Files: GPX, KML
  • Documents: PDF (for certain endpoints)

docs.title: File Size Limits
docs.text:
• Profile avatars: 5MB
  • Car images: 5MB
  • Trip images: 10MB
  • Track files: 2MB

docs.title: System Time
docs.text:
• GET /api/systemtime/
    • Returns the current server time in Asia/Dubai (UTC+4). Useful for synchronizing client clocks with the API.
    • Authentication: Optional (public endpoint).

Example Response:

{
    "currentTime": "2026-03-31T14:30:00+04:00"
}

docs.title: Field Validators
docs.text:
• POST /api/validators/
    • Validates email, username, and/or phone fields for uniqueness before registration. Useful for real-time form validation.
    • Authentication: Not required (public endpoint).

Request Body: Include one or more fields to validate:

{
    "email": "user@example.com",
    "username": "newuser",
    "phone": "+971501234567"
}

Example Response:

{
    "email": {
        "valid": true
    },
    "username": {
        "valid": false,
        "error": "Username is already taken"
    },
    "phone": {
        "valid": true
    }
}

Only the fields you provide in the request are validated and returned in the response. The phone field uses Django's PhoneNumberField for format validation.

docs.title: Best Practices
docs.text:
1. Always use HTTPS in production
  2. Store JWT tokens securely (not in localStorage for web apps)
  3. Refresh tokens before they expire
  4. Handle token expiration gracefully
  5. Use pagination for large datasets
  6. Implement proper error handling
  7. Validate data on the client side before sending
  8. Use appropriate HTTP methods (GET, POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE)
  9. Include proper Content-Type headers
  10. Test with the Swagger UI at /docs/swagger-ui/

docs.title: "Given token not valid for any token type"
docs.text:
Cause: Token is expired, invalid, or malformed

Solutions: 1. Refresh the token using /api/token/refresh/ 2. Re-authenticate with username and password 3. Check token format (should start with eyJ...)

docs.title: "Authentication credentials were not provided"
docs.text:
Cause: Missing or malformed Authorization header

Solutions: 1. Ensure header is present: Authorization: Bearer <token> 2. Check for typos in "Bearer" (case-sensitive) 3. Verify token is not empty or None

docs.title: "nopermissiontoperformaction"
docs.text:
Cause: User lacks required permission for the action

Solutions: 1. Check user has correct group membership 2. Verify permission exists in PermissionMatrix 3. Contact administrator for elevated permissions

docs.title: Field shows "This field is required" but value is provided
docs.text:
Causes: 1. Wrong field name (camelCase vs snake_case mismatch) 2. Field not expected by this endpoint/method 3. Type mismatch (string vs number)

Solutions: 1. Use camelCase for API requests (e.g., startTime not start_time) 2. Check Swagger documentation for accepted fields 3. Verify data type matches expected format

docs.title: 503 Service Unavailable
docs.text:
Cause: Either (a) an intentional maintenance window, triggered via the nginx-level toggle (infra/enable_maintenance_mode.sh), or (b) transient backend unavailability (upstream down, gunicorn restart, failed nginx health check).

Solutions: 1. If the response includes a Retry-After header (currently 3600 during intentional maintenance), back off for at least that many seconds before retrying. 2. Check Club News for announced downtime windows. 3. See Maintenance Mode for the full mechanism and recommended client behaviour.

Note: There is no Django-level maintenance mode — 503 responses always originate from the nginx layer, either from the deliberate maintenance toggle or from an upstream failure. Clients should match on 503 + Retry-After to detect a deliberate maintenance state, and treat it as a transient operational state rather than an application error (do not send to Sentry).

docs.title: "count": 0 with no results
docs.text:
Causes: 1. No data matching filter criteria 2. Page number exceeds available pages 3. Authentication required for filtered results

Solutions: 1. Remove filters to see all data 2. Request page 1 if using page numbers 3. Verify authentication token

docs.title: Next/Previous URLs are null
docs.text: Null next: You are on the last page Null previous: You are on the first page

docs.title: Requests returning 429 Too Many Requests
docs.text:
Cause: Exceeded rate limit (100 requests/minute per IP)

Solutions: 1. Implement exponential backoff 2. Reduce request frequency 3. Cache responses locally

See Rate Limiting for details.

docs.title: Trip times appearing incorrect
docs.text:
Cause: Client not parsing timezone correctly

Solutions: 1. All API times are in Asia/Dubai (UTC+4) 2. Parse with timezone awareness 3. Examples: 2026-03-15T07:00:00+04:00

docs.title: "Request is not a multipart request"
docs.text:
Cause: Wrong Content-Type for file upload

Solutions: 1. Use multipart/form-data not application/json 2. Do not JSON-encode the body 3. Use appropriate HTTP client settings

docs.title: File too large (413 Payload Too Large)
docs.text:
Cause: File exceeds size limit

Solutions: 1. Compress images before upload 2. Stay within limits: - Profile avatars: 5MB - Car images: 5MB - Trip images: 10MB - Track files: 2MB

docs.title: Common HTTP Status Codes
docs.text: Code Meaning Common Causes 200 OK Successful request 201 Created Resource successfully created 400 Bad Request Invalid data, validation errors 401 Unauthorized Missing or invalid token 403 Forbidden Permission denied 404 Not Found Resource doesn't exist 422 Unprocessable Business rule violation 429 Too Many Requests Rate limit exceeded 500 Internal Server Error Server error, check logs 503 Service Unavailable Maintenance mode

docs.title: Getting Help
docs.text:
1. Check Swagger UI at /docs/swagger-ui/ for interactive testing
  2. Review error messages in response body
  3. Check server logs for detailed error information
  4. Contact support via the feedback system

docs.title: Authentication and Profiles
docs.text:
This document outlines the API endpoints for user authentication, registration, and profile management.

For a high-level overview of the authentication process, please refer to the API Concepts document.

docs.title: Registration and Password Management
docs.text: The API provides endpoints for user registration and password management, powered by the rest_registration library.

docs.title: Registration
docs.text:
POST /api/auth/register/

The request body should include the user's details as defined by the MemberRegistrationSerializer.

Request Body:

{
    "username": "newuser",
    "email": "user@example.com",
    "firstName": "John",
    "lastName": "Doe",
    "phone": "0501234567",
    "password": "securePassword123",
    "password2": "securePassword123",
    "dob": "1990-01-15",
    "iceName": "Jane Doe",
    "icePhone": "0507654321",
    "gender": "M",
    "nationality": "AE",
    "city": "Dubai",
    "carBrand": "TO",
    "carModel": "Land Cruiser",
    "carColor": "White",
    "carYear": 2022
}

Fields:

Field Type Required Description username string Yes Unique username email string Yes Email address firstName string No First name lastName string No Last name phone string No Phone number password string Yes Password password2 string Yes Password confirmation (must match password) dob date No Date of birth (YYYY-MM-DD) iceName string No Emergency contact name icePhone string No Emergency contact phone gender string No Gender code (M, F, O) nationality string No Country code (e.g., "AE") city string No City name avatar file No Profile image (multipart/form-data) carBrand string No 2-letter car brand code (e.g., "TO" for Toyota). If provided, a Vehicle is automatically created. carModel string No Car model name carColor string No Car color carYear integer No Car year of manufacture

Note: The carBrand, carModel, carColor, and carYear fields are write-only. When provided during registration, a Vehicle record is automatically created and set as the member's primary vehicle. See Vehicles for managing vehicles after registration.

docs.title: Change Password
docs.text:
Authenticated users can change their password by making a POST request to /api/auth/change-password/.

POST /api/auth/change-password/

Request Body:

{
    "oldPassword": "current_password",
    "password": "new_password",
    "passwordConfirm": "new_password"
}

Fields:

Field Type Required Description oldPassword string Yes Current password password string Yes New password passwordConfirm string Yes New password confirmation (must match password)

Note: The API accepts camelCase field names. The underlying serializer fields are old_password, password, and password_confirm.

Note: password and passwordConfirm must match.

Important: When a user changes their password, all existing JWT tokens are automatically invalidated. Users will need to log in again with their new password to obtain a fresh token.

docs.title: Other Endpoints
docs.text:
The rest_registration library also provides endpoints for: * Resetting a forgotten password * Verifying registration via email

Please refer to the library's documentation for details on these flows.

docs.title: Retrieving a Profile
docs.text:
To retrieve a user's profile, make a GET request to /api/members/{id}/.

GET /api/members/{id}/

Success Response: The response will be a JSON object containing the user's profile information. The fields returned are defined by the ProfileSerializer.

Note: While the serializer and database use snake_case for field names (e.g., first_name), the API will return camelCase in the response body (e.g., firstName).

{
    "id": 1,
    "username": "testuser",
    "email": "test@example.com",
    "firstName": "Test",
    "lastName": "User",
    "phone": "1234567890",
    "dob": "2000-01-01",
    "iceName": "Jane Doe",
    "icePhone": "0987654321",
    "level": {
        "id": 1,
        "name": "Newbie",
        "numericLevel": 10,
        "minTripsForUpgrade": 5
    },
    "tripCount": 5,
    "avatar": null,
    "permissions": [
        {
            "id": 1,
            "action": "search_members",
            "levels": []
        }
    ],
    "paidMember": true,
    "dateJoined": "2026-01-01T12:00:00",
    "city": "Dubai",
    "gender": "M",
    "nationality": "AE",
    "title": "",
    "lastVisited": "2026-03-30T14:22:00Z"
}

Note: The profile response does NOT include vehicle/car fields. Vehicles are managed separately via the Vehicles endpoints.

Note on permissions: Each entry has an action field containing the lowercase DB value of the action (e.g., "search_members", "create_trip"). The levels field contains an array of level objects ({id, name, numericLevel, minTripsForUpgrade}) for permissions that are restricted to specific levels. An empty levels array means the permission applies to all levels.

docs.title: Updating a Profile
docs.text:
To update a user's profile, make a PATCH request to /api/members/{id}/. Users can only update their own profiles unless they are an administrator.

PATCH /api/members/{id}/

Request Body: The request body should contain the fields to be updated. Note that some fields like username, email, level, tripCount, paidMember, and lastVisited are read-only.

Editable Fields: firstName, lastName, phone, city, dob, iceName, icePhone, gender, nationality, avatar, title

Success Response: A successful update will return a 200 OK status code and the updated profile data.

docs.title: Generate Firebase Custom Token
docs.text:
• POST /api/firebase/custom-token

    Note: This endpoint does NOT use a trailing slash.

    • Generates a Firebase custom authentication token for the authenticated user. This can be used by clients to authenticate with Firebase services (e.g., real-time database, Cloud Messaging).
    • Authentication: Required (Bearer token).

Example Request:

curl -X POST "http://localhost:8000/api/firebase/custom-token" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <your-token>"

Success Response (200 OK):

{
    "firebaseToken": "eyJhbGciOiJSUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9...",
    "expiresIn": 3600
}
Field Type Description firebaseToken string Firebase custom token (JWT) expiresIn integer Token expiry in seconds (3600 = 1 hour)

Error Response (500 Internal Server Error):

{
    "detail": "Firebase error: <error_message>"
}

This error occurs if the Firebase Admin SDK is not initialized or encounters an error during token creation.

docs.title: Background Tasks
docs.text:
The AD4x4 backend uses Huey (a lightweight task queue) for asynchronous background processing. Background tasks handle operations that should not block HTTP requests, such as:

  • Sending notifications (push, email, Telegram)
  • Syncing with external services (Gallery system)
  • Periodic cleanup operations
  • Delayed processing

docs.title: Huey Configuration
docs.text:
Huey is configured in ad4x4/settings.py:

HUEY = {
    'huey_class': 'huey.RedisHuey',
    'connection': {
        'host': os.getenv('REDIS_HOST'),
        'port': os.getenv('REDIS_PORT'),
        'password': os.getenv('REDIS_PASSWORD'),
    },
    'consumer': {
        'workers': 1,
        'worker_type': 'thread',
        'scheduler_interval': 1,
        'periodic': True,
    },
}

docs.title: Task Types
docs.text: Decorator Use Case Example @task One-time async task Sending a notification @periodic_task Scheduled recurring task Daily cleanup at 3 AM

docs.title: Running the Task Consumer
docs.text:
The Huey consumer must be running for background tasks to execute:

python manage.py run_huey

Important: This command blocks and runs continuously. Run it in a terminal, supervisor, or systemd service.

docs.title: Consumer Options
docs.text:
python manage.py run_huey \
  --worker-type=thread \      # or 'process'
  --workers=1 \               # number of workers (production runs with 1)
  --scheduler_interval=1      # scheduler check interval (seconds)

docs.title: Notification Tasks
docs.text: Task Trigger Retry Policy send_trip_notification Trip published 2 retries, 5min delay send_trip_approval_notification Trip approved/declined 2 retries, 5min delay send_registration_from_waitlist_notification Waitlist promotion 2 retries, 15min delay send_removed_from_trip_registered_notification Registration removal 2 retries, 15min delay send_removed_from_trip_waitlist_notification Waitlist removal 2 retries, 15min delay send_upgrade_request_handled_notification Upgrade request decision 2 retries, 5min delay send_upgrade_request_created_notification New upgrade request 2 retries, 5min delay send_club_news ClubNews status → APPROVED 2 retries, 5min delay send_feedback_notification Feedback submission 2 retries, 5min delay send_new_trip_comment_notification_task New trip comment 2 retries, 5min delay

docs.title: Gallery Sync Tasks
docs.text: Task Trigger Retry Policy create_gallery_for_trip_task Trip approval 6 retries, 1hr delay update_gallery_for_trip_task Trip update 6 retries, 1hr delay delete_gallery_for_trip_task Trip deletion (soft) 3 retries, 1hr delay restore_gallery_for_trip_task Trip restoration 3 retries, 1hr delay

docs.title: Periodic Tasks
docs.text: Task Schedule Description process_account_deletion_requests Daily at 12 AM Processes accounts pending deletion after 3-day grace period cleanup_expired_geocoding_cache Daily at 1 AM Removes expired geocoding cache entries periodic_purge_inactive_devices Daily at 2 AM Removes inactive FCM devices (30+ days old) periodic_delete_old_triprequests Daily at 3 AM Deletes trip requests older than 1 day periodic_purge_old_notifications Daily at 4 AM Deletes notification logs older than 60 days periodic_upgrade_request_reminder Daily at 8 PM Sends reminder notifications for pending upgrade requests

docs.title: Cron Expressions
docs.text:
Tasks use crontab-style scheduling:

@periodic_task(crontab(minute='0', hour='20'))
def daily_reminder():
    pass

Crontab Parameters: | Parameter | Values | |-----------|--------| | minute | 0-59 or '' | | hour | 0-23 or '' | | day | 1-31 or '' | | month | 1-12 or '' | | day_of_week | 0-6 (Monday-Sunday) or '*' |

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
# Every day at 8 PM
@periodic_task(crontab(minute='0', hour='20'))

# Every hour at minute 30
@periodic_task(crontab(minute='30', hour='*'))

# Every Monday at 9 AM
@periodic_task(crontab(minute='0', hour='9', day_of_week='1'))

# Every 15 minutes
@periodic_task(crontab(minute='*/15'))

docs.title: Retry Configuration
docs.text:
Tasks can be configured with retries:

@task(retries=3, retry_delay=3600)  # 3 retries, 1 hour between
def fragile_task(data):
    pass

Retry Parameters: | Parameter | Description | |-----------|-------------| | retries | Maximum retry attempts (default: varies) | | retry_delay | Seconds to wait between retries (default: varies) |

docs.title: Logging
docs.text:
All background task logging goes to the ad4x4-worker logger:

import logging
logger = logging.getLogger('ad4x4-worker')

logger.info(f'Processing {count} items')
logger.error(f'Failed to process: {str(e)}')

docs.title: Monitoring
docs.text: Check task execution in: 1. Application logs 2. Django admin (failed task records) 3. Redis (task queue status)

docs.title: List Pending Tasks
docs.text:
# In Django shell
from huey.contrib.djhuey import huey
print(huey.pending())  # Returns pending task count

docs.title: Run Task Immediately
docs.text:
from api.background import send_trip_notification
send_trip_notification(trip)  # Schedules async execution

docs.title: Test Task Synchronously
docs.text: For testing, tasks can be executed synchronously by setting immediate=True in settings or using huey's testing mode.

docs.title: Consumer Not Running
docs.text: Symptom: Notifications not sent, galleries not created Fix: Start the consumer: python manage.py run_huey

docs.title: Tasks Stuck in Queue
docs.text: Symptom: Tasks accumulating, not processing Fix: Check Redis connection and consumer logs

docs.title: Task Failures
docs.text: Symptom: Same task failing repeatedly Fix: Check logs for error details; fix underlying issue; manually retry

docs.title: High Memory Usage
docs.text: Symptom: Worker consuming too much memory Fix: Reduce workers count or use process worker type instead of thread

docs.title: Club News
docs.text: This document outlines the club news (announcements) system.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Club news allows administrators to publish announcements visible to all members. News items go through a status workflow: Draft -> Approved -> Sent.

docs.title: List Club News
docs.text:
• GET /api/clubnews/
  • Authentication: Optional (public endpoint)
  • Permission: None required

Only items with status SENT are returned, ordered by submitDate descending.

Query Parameters: - page - Page number (default: 1) - page_size - Results per page (default: 20)

Response:

{
  "count": 5,
  "next": null,
  "previous": null,
  "results": [
    {
      "id": 1,
      "title": "New Trip Guidelines",
      "content": "Please review the updated trip guidelines...",
      "submitDate": "2026-03-15T10:00:00",
      "status": "SENT",
      "levels": [1, 2],
      "image": "/media/clubnews/2026/03/guidelines.jpg"
    }
  ]
}

docs.title: Retrieve Club News
docs.text:
• GET /api/clubnews/{id}/

Response:

{
  "id": 1,
  "title": "New Trip Guidelines",
  "content": "Please review the updated trip guidelines for the upcoming season.",
  "submitDate": "2026-03-15T10:00:00",
  "status": "SENT",
  "levels": [1, 2],
  "image": "/media/clubnews/2026/03/guidelines.jpg"
}

docs.title: Response Fields
docs.text:
Field Type Description id integer Unique identifier title string News title (max 100 characters) content string Full news content submitDate datetime When the news was approved/published status string Status code (only SENT items are returned via API) levels array Array of Level IDs this news targets. Empty means all members. image string Optional image URL

Note: The API does NOT include an author field. News items are managed by administrators via Django Admin.

docs.title: Status Workflow
docs.text:
Status Description DRAFT Initial state, not visible to members APPROVED Approved, submitDate is set automatically SENT Notifications have been sent, visible via API ERROR Error occurred during notification sending

Note: Once a news item has status SENT, it cannot be modified.

docs.title: Notifications
docs.text:
When new club news is published, a notification is sent to all members with the CLUB_NEWS notification type enabled. If levels are specified, only members at those levels receive the notification.

docs.title: Editable Strings (UIString) API
docs.text: This document outlines how to use the Editable Strings (UIString) API to manage translations for the application.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: The UIString feature allows for dynamic management of strings in the application's UI. Strings are stored as key-value pairs, with support for English and Arabic translations. The API provides endpoints for creating, retrieving, updating, and deleting these strings.

docs.title: Authentication
docs.text: GET (read) endpoints are public — no authentication required. POST, PUT, PATCH, and DELETE endpoints require authentication and the EDIT_UI_STRINGS permission.

docs.title: Retrieve a UI String
docs.text:
• GET /api/strings/{key}/

    Retrieves a single UI string by its key.

    Parameters:

    • key (string): The key of the UI string to retrieve.
    • lang (string, optional): The language to retrieve. Can be en or ar. Defaults to en.

    Example Request:

    bash curl -X GET "https://example.com/api/strings/welcome_message/?lang=ar"

    Example Response:

    json { "key": "welcome_message", "values": { "title": "مرحباً", "body": "مرحباً بك في تطبيقنا!" } }

docs.title: Create a UI String
docs.text:
• POST /api/strings/

    Creates a new UI string.

    Example Request:

    bash curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{ "key": "new_feature_announcement", "values_en": { "title": "New Feature!", "description": "We have a new feature for you to try." }, "values_ar": { "title": "ميزة جديدة!", "description": "لدينا ميزة جديدة لتجربتها." } }' "https://example.com/api/strings/"

docs.title: Update a UI String
docs.text:
• PUT or PATCH /api/strings/{key}/

    Updates an existing UI string.

    Example Request (PUT):

    bash curl -X PUT -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{ "key": "welcome_message", "values_en": { "title": "Welcome", "body": "Welcome to our app!" }, "values_ar": { "title": "أهلاً بك", "body": "أهلاً بك في تطبيقنا!" } }' "https://example.com/api/strings/welcome_message/"

    Example Request (PATCH):

    bash curl -X PATCH -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{ "values_en": { "title": "Welcome Back", "body": "Welcome back to our app!" } }' "https://example.com/api/strings/welcome_message/"

docs.title: Delete a UI String
docs.text:
• DELETE /api/strings/{key}/

    Deletes a UI string.

    Example Request:

    bash curl -X DELETE -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" "https://example.com/api/strings/welcome_message/"

docs.title: Validation Rules
docs.text:
The following validation rules apply when creating or updating UI strings:

  • key: A unique string used to identify the UI string. This field is required when creating a new string and cannot be changed after creation.
  • values_en: A JSON object containing the English translations. This field is required, and its keys define the structure that values_ar must follow.
  • values_ar: A JSON object containing the Arabic translations. This field is optional and can be null or an empty JSON object ({}). If values_ar is provided and is not empty, it must contain the exact same set of keys as values_en.

docs.title: Feedback System
docs.text: This document describes the feedback submission API. It lets authenticated members report bugs, request features, ask for help, or send general comments. Each submission is stored in the database and a notification is dispatched to administrators via the configured channels (Telegram / email / push).

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Model Feedback (api/models/models_feedback.py) Serializer FeedbackSerializer (inline in api/views/views_feedback.py) Create endpoint POST /api/feedback/ (router-registered FeedbackCreateAPIView) List-by-member endpoint GET /api/members/{id}/feedback — no trailing slash Notification task send_feedback_notification — Huey @task, 2 retries, 5-minute delay

docs.title: Model Fields
docs.text: Wire field (camelCase) Internal (snake_case) Type Required on create Returned by the API Notes feedbackType feedback_type enum (see below) No — defaults to general Yes One of bug, feature, general, support message message string Yes Yes Free-form text; TextField with no enforced length limit image image file (image) No Yes (as an absolute URL, or null) Single image; see File Uploads (set server-side) user member FK n/a — auto-filled from the authenticated user not returned (set server-side) timestamp datetime n/a — auto_now_add not returned Used for default ordering (newest first)

docs.title: Feedback Types
docs.text:
Value (wire + DB) Label (for UI display) bug Bug Report feature Feature Request general General Feedback (default if omitted) support Help / Support

The API accepts and returns the code ("bug"), never the label. If your UI needs the human-readable label, map the code client-side — the label is not exposed by a /api/choices/ endpoint.

docs.title: 1. Submit Feedback
docs.text:
POST /api/feedback/

Authentication Bearer JWT required Permission Any authenticated user Throttle 200 req/min per authenticated user — see Rate Limiting Content-Type application/json or multipart/form-data (use multipart only when attaching an image)

docs.title: Request body (JSON — no image)
docs.text:
{
    "feedbackType": "bug",
    "message": "The trip registration button is unresponsive on iOS 17."
}

docs.title: Request body (multipart/form-data — with image)
docs.text:
curl -X POST https://ap.ad4x4.com/api/feedback/ \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_TOKEN" \
  -F "feedbackType=bug" \
  -F "message=Registration button unresponsive on iOS 17" \
  -F "image=@screenshot.png"

camelCase applies to multipart form fields, not just JSON. DRF's CamelCaseMultiPartParser and CamelCaseJSONParser (wired into DEFAULT_PARSER_CLASSES in ad4x4/settings.py) translate the wire-format feedbackType into the internal feedback_type for you. Do not send feedback_type in multipart — the parser will treat it as an unknown field and drop it, which leads to the default (general) being saved instead.

docs.title: Success response (201 Created)
docs.text:
{
    "success": true,
    "message": {
        "feedbackType": "bug",
        "message": "The trip registration button is unresponsive on iOS 17.",
        "image": "https://ap.ad4x4.com/uploads/feedback_images/2026/04/screenshot_3f4a2b8c.png"
    }
}
  • image is null when the submission didn't include one.
  • user and timestamp are recorded on the server but deliberately not returned — the client already knows who submitted it, and the server time is not exposed.

docs.title: Error response (400 Bad Request — validation failure)
docs.text:
{
    "success": false,
    "message": {
        "feedbackType": ["\"invalid\" is not a valid choice."],
        "message": ["This field is required."]
    }
}

On validation failure, the message field holds DRF's standard error dict, keyed by the offending wire-format field name. Keys are camelCased.

docs.title: Error response (401 Unauthorized)
docs.text:
{
    "success": false,
    "message": "authentication_credentials_were_not_provided"
}

Returned when the Authorization header is missing, the JWT is expired, or the user's token_version has been bumped (e.g. after a password change — all prior tokens are invalidated, see API Concepts).

docs.title: 2. List a Member's Feedback
docs.text:
GET /api/members/{id}/feedback — no trailing slash

Authentication Bearer JWT required Permission You may read your own feedback only ({id} must match your own member ID), unless you are a superuser — in which case any member's feedback is visible. Regular permission-matrix roles do not grant access. Response Paginated — uses the project-wide StandardResultsSetPagination

Returns the feedback items submitted by the specified member, most recent first.

docs.title: Query parameters
docs.text: Parameter Type Default Description page integer 1 Page number to retrieve page_size integer 20 Items per page (max 500). Note: query-string parameters are not camelCase-converted — use the snake_case name here.

docs.title: Response (200 OK)
docs.text:
This endpoint uses the standard DRF pagination envelope, not the {success, message} wrapper used by the create endpoint:

{
    "count": 27,
    "next": "https://ap.ad4x4.com/api/members/42/feedback?page=2",
    "previous": null,
    "results": [
        {
            "feedbackType": "bug",
            "message": "Still broken on iOS 17",
            "image": null
        },
        {
            "feedbackType": "feature",
            "message": "Would love a dark mode option",
            "image": "https://ap.ad4x4.com/uploads/feedback_images/2026/04/mockup_8d2e1f0a.png"
        }
    ]
}

docs.title: Error responses
docs.text:
• 401 Unauthorized — missing or invalid JWT (same shape as the create endpoint).
  • 403 Forbidden — authenticated, but trying to read another member's feedback without superuser privileges: json { "detail": "You do not have permission to perform this action." } (This endpoint emits DRF's default {"detail": ...} on 403, not the unified {success, message} envelope. Frontend code should handle both shapes.)
  • 404 Not Found — no member exists with the given {id}.

docs.title: File Uploads
docs.text: Wire field image (single file — the model has one ImageField, not a many-to-many relation) Content-Type multipart/form-data (required only when attaching an image; otherwise send JSON) Accepted formats Anything Pillow can decode — JPEG, PNG, WebP, GIF, BMP, TIFF. Django's ImageField verifies that the upload is a real image and rejects other file types with a 400. Size limit No size validation is performed in Django. The effective cap is 20 MB, imposed by nginx's client_max_body_size 20M (infra/nginx/secure/default.conf.template:66). Uploads larger than that will be rejected by nginx with a 413 Payload Too Large before the request reaches Django. Resize or recompress client-side for large screenshots.

docs.title: Storage path
docs.text:
Uploaded files are stored inside the app container at:

/app/uploads/feedback_images/{YYYY}/{MM}/{originalBasename}_{8-char-hex}{ext}
  • {YYYY}/{MM} is the upload month (server time, Asia/Dubai).
  • {originalBasename} is the filename the client sent, minus the extension.
  • {8-char-hex} is uuid.uuid4().hex[:8]. It uniquifies concurrent uploads that happen to share the same filename, but it is not cryptographically unpredictable — do not treat it as a secret.
  • The same file is served over HTTP at https://ap.ad4x4.com/uploads/feedback_images/... via a custom serve_media view (Whitenoise only serves the static assets under /static/; the /uploads/ path is handled separately so that authentication can be layered on later if needed).

Example: a client upload of screenshot.png in April 2026 is stored as feedback_images/2026/04/screenshot_3f4a2b8c.png.

docs.title: Notifications
docs.text:
After a feedback record is saved, FeedbackCreateAPIView.perform_create dispatches the Huey task background.send_feedback_notification(feedback_instance). The task assembles a notification with the feedback type, message, and (if present) the image URL, and delivers it to the administrators configured in ConfigurableSettings via the notification service — email, Telegram, and/or push, depending on which channels are enabled.

Task name send_feedback_notification Defined in api/background.py Retries 2 Retry delay 300 seconds (5 minutes) Runs in The huey Docker container (production) / synchronously (development)

See Background Tasks and Notifications for the full notification pipeline.

docs.title: Practical Notes for Frontend Implementers
docs.text:
• Two different response envelopes on this page. The create endpoint returns {success, message}; the list-by-member endpoint returns the standard DRF {count, next, previous, results} pagination envelope. Your client must handle both shapes — don't assume every endpoint uses the success wrapper.
  • Don't rely on timestamp in the response — it isn't returned. If you need to show "submitted X minutes ago" in the UI, use the local Date.now() at send time and cache it client-side, or fall back to refreshing the member-feedback list.
  • Default feedback type is general. Omitting feedbackType is valid and results in a "General Feedback" submission. If your UI forces the user to pick, this is a safe fallback for the "other" option.
  • Image URL is absolute. DRF builds the full https://... URL using the request host, so you can use it directly in an <img src> without extra prefixing.
  • Rate limiting applies. A burst of 200+ feedback submissions per minute from the same user will hit the DRF throttle and return 429 Too Many Requests.

docs.title: Gallery System Configuration
docs.text: The gallery system provides media management for trip photos. Galleries are synced with an external Gallery API, and all sync operations happen asynchronously via background tasks.

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text:
Trip Approved
    ↓
Background Task: create_gallery_for_trip_task
    ↓
GalleryWebhookService.create_gallery_for_trip()
    ↓
External Gallery API
    ↓
Response stored in Trip.gallery_id

docs.title: Configuration Fields
docs.text: Setting Type Description gallery_api_url String Base URL for the external Gallery API gallery_api_timeout Integer Timeout in seconds for API calls (default: 10) enable_gallery_system Boolean Master switch to enable/disable all gallery features auto_create_trip_gallery Boolean Auto-create gallery when trip is approved allow_manual_gallery_creation Boolean Allow clients to show manual creation UI

docs.title: Gallery ID Storage
docs.text:
When a gallery is successfully created for a trip, the external gallery ID is stored in:

trip.gallery_id = "<external_gallery_id>"
trip.save(update_fields=['gallery_id'])

This allows the system to reference the gallery for future updates.

docs.title: Create Gallery
docs.text: Trigger: Trip approval Task: create_gallery_for_trip_task(trip_id) Retry Policy: 6 retries, 1 hour delay between retries

docs.title: Update Gallery
docs.text: Trigger: Trip details change Task: update_gallery_for_trip_task(trip_id) Retry Policy: 6 retries, 1 hour delay between retries

docs.title: Delete Gallery
docs.text: Trigger: Trip soft-delete Task: delete_gallery_for_trip_task(trip_id) Retry Policy: 3 retries, 1 hour delay between retries

docs.title: Restore Gallery
docs.text: Trigger: Trip restoration Task: restore_gallery_for_trip_task(trip_id) Retry Policy: 3 retries, 1 hour delay between retries

docs.title: Retry Logic
docs.text:
All gallery tasks retry with a fixed 1-hour delay between attempts (not exponential backoff). Huey's retry_delay is a constant for a given @task decorator:

  • create_gallery_for_trip_task — up to 6 retries, 1-hour delay each (total window ≈ 6 hours)
  • update_gallery_for_trip_task — up to 6 retries, 1-hour delay each
  • delete_gallery_for_trip_task — up to 3 retries, 1-hour delay each
  • restore_gallery_for_trip_task — up to 3 retries, 1-hour delay each

After all retries are exhausted, the task stops and logs an error. Manual intervention may be required.

docs.title: Logging
docs.text:
Gallery operations log to the ad4x4-web logger (see api/services/gallery_webhook.py):

# Success
logger.info(f"Gallery ID {gallery_id} saved to trip {trip.id}")

# Failure
logger.warning(f"Gallery creation failed for trip {trip.id}, will retry")

# Error
logger.error(f"Trip {trip_id} not found when creating gallery")

docs.title: Manual Test
docs.text:
from api.services.gallery_webhook import GalleryWebhookService
from api.models import Trip

trip = Trip.objects.first()
gallery_id = GalleryWebhookService.create_gallery_for_trip(trip)
print(f"Created gallery: {gallery_id}")

docs.title: Disable for Testing
docs.text: Set enable_gallery_system = False in Global Settings to prevent API calls during testing.

docs.title: Displaying Galleries
docs.text:
1. Check if trip.gallery_id exists
  2. Construct gallery URL using the external Gallery API base URL
  3. Display gallery iframe or link

docs.title: Manual Creation Flag
docs.text: Respect allow_manual_gallery_creation to show/hide "Create Gallery" buttons in the UI.

docs.title: Gallery Not Created
docs.text: Symptom: Trip approved but no gallery_id on trip Causes: - Gallery system disabled (enable_gallery_system = False) - External API unreachable - Task failed all retries Fix: Check logs, verify settings, manually trigger gallery creation

docs.title: Gallery Sync Failures
docs.text: Symptom: Repeated failures in logs Causes: - Invalid API credentials - Network issues - External API down Fix: Verify credentials, check external API status, check Huey consumer running

docs.title: HERE Maps Integration
docs.text: This document outlines the configuration and API endpoints for the HERE Maps reverse geocoding feature.

docs.title: Admin Configuration
docs.text:
The HERE Maps integration is configured through the Global Settings in the Django Admin interface. The following fields are available:

  • Here Maps Enabled: Master switch to enable or disable the entire HERE Maps feature.
  • Here Maps Api Key: Your HERE Maps API key.
  • Here Maps Api Base Url: The base URL for the HERE Maps reverse geocoding API.
  • Here Maps Selected Fields: A JSON list of fields to be returned by the reverse geocoding endpoint (e.g., ["city", "district"]).
  • Here Maps Max Fields: The maximum number of fields to display in the formatted area string.
  • Here Maps Available Fields: A JSON array of objects defining the available fields and their display names (e.g., [{"name": "city", "displayName": "City"}, {"name": "district", "displayName": "District"}]).
  • Here Maps Cache Duration: The duration, in minutes, for which geocoding results are cached in the database (default: 1440 minutes = 1 day).
  • Here Maps Request Timeout: The timeout, in seconds, for requests to the HERE Maps API.

docs.title: Get HERE Maps Configuration
docs.text:
This public endpoint provides the necessary configuration for the frontend to interact with the HERE Maps feature.

  • Endpoint: GET /api/settings/here-maps-config/
  • Authentication: None
  • Response: json { "enabled": true, "selectedFields": ["district", "city"], "maxFields": 2, "availableFields": [ {"name": "title", "displayName": "Place Name"}, {"name": "district", "displayName": "District"}, {"name": "city", "displayName": "City"} ] }

docs.title: Reverse Geocode Coordinates
docs.text:
This endpoint takes a latitude and longitude and returns a formatted area string based on the configured selectedFields and maxFields.

  • Endpoint: POST /api/geocoding/reverse/
  • Authentication: Required
  • Request Body: json { "latitude": 24.4539, "longitude": 54.3773 }
  • Responses:
    • 200 OK: json { "success": true, "area": "Al Ain, Abu Dhabi", "fields": { "district": "Al Ain", "city": "Abu Dhabi" }, "cached": false }
    • 400 Bad Request: If latitude or longitude are missing or invalid.
    • 401 Unauthorized: If the user is not authenticated.
    • 500 Internal Server Error: If there is an error communicating with the HERE Maps API.

docs.title: Lead Trip History Search
docs.text: This endpoint allows searching for trips where a member was the trip lead or deputy lead. Returns full trip details with lead information and user registration status.

docs.title: Endpoint
docs.text:
URL: GET /api/trips/lead-trip-history?lead_id={member_id}

Authentication: Required (Bearer token) Permission Required: Users must have VIEW_TRIPS_AS_LEAD permission to access this endpoint.

docs.title: Query Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Type Required Description lead_id integer Yes Member ID to filter for trips where this member was the lead or deputy lead level integer No Numeric trip level for filtering to include only trips at a specific level min_level integer No Minimum level numeric value for filtering to include only trips at this level or higher (inclusive) max_level integer No Maximum level numeric value for filtering to include only trips at this level or lower (inclusive) start_time_min date (ISO 8601) No Filter for trips starting from this date (inclusive) start_time_max date (ISO 8601) No Filter for trips starting until this date (inclusive) meeting_point integer No Filter by meeting point ID area string No Filter by meeting point area code (e.g., DXB, AUH) order string No Order results by "starttimedesc" (most recent first, default) or "starttimeasc" (oldest first) page integer No Page number (default: 1) page_size integer No Number of results per page (default: 20, max: 500)

docs.title: Request Examples
docs.text:
Basic search - get all trips where member was lead:

curl -X GET "http://api.example.com/api/trips/lead-trip-history?lead_id=21144" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <your-token>"

Filter by specific level:

curl -X GET "http://api.example.com/api/trips/lead-trip-history?lead_id=21144&level=10" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <your-token>"

Filter by minimum level (Newbie and above):

curl -X GET "http://api.example.com/api/trips/lead-trip-history?lead_id=21144&min_level=10" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <your-token>"

Filter by maximum level (Newbie and below):

curl -X GET "http://api.example.com/api/trips/lead-trip-history?lead_id=21144&max_level=10" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <your-token>"

Filter by date range:

curl -X GET "http://api.example.com/api/trips/lead-trip-history?lead_id=21144&start_time_min=2024-01-01&start_time_max=2024-12-31" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <your-token>"

Order oldest first:

curl -X GET "http://api.example.com/api/trips/lead-trip-history?lead_id=21144&order=start_time_asc" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <your-token>"

Paginated results:

curl -X GET "http://api.example.com/api/trips/lead-trip-history?lead_id=21144&page=2&page_size=10" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <your-token>"

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• Lead/Deputy Lead: The endpoint checks if the specified member was the primary lead OR a deputy lead for the trip
  • Authentication Required: All users must be authenticated
  • Permission: Access is granted if: (1) the user is a superuser, or (2) the user has the VIEW_TRIPS_AS_LEAD permission granted through the permission matrix.
  • Level Filtering: Uses level (exact match), min_level (minimum inclusive), or max_level (maximum inclusive)
  • Example: level=10 returns only Newbie level trips
  • Example: min_level=10 returns Newbie and above
  • Example: max_level=100 returns Newbie and Intermediate levels
  • Date Filtering: Filters by start_time field. Uses date-only comparison (ignores time component).
  • start_time_min: Trips starting on or after this date
  • start_time_max: Trips starting on or before this date
  • Default Ordering: Results are ordered by start_time descending (most recent first). Can be overridden with order=start_time_asc for oldest first.
  • Pagination: Standard pagination with 20 items per page (configurable up to 500).
  • Response Fields: Includes full trip details via ListTripSerializer:
  • Basic trip info (title, description, dates, capacity, approval status)
  • Lead information (id, username)
  • Level (id, name, numericLevel, displayName)
  • Meeting point (id, name, lat, lon, area, link) if associated
  • User registration status for authenticated user (isRegistered, isWaitlisted)
  • Waitlist and registered counts
  • Gallery ID if available
  • Permission Check: The HasViewTripsAsLeadPermission checks:
  • If user is not authenticated - denies access
  • If user is superuser - allows access
  • If user has the VIEW_TRIPS_AS_LEAD action in the permission matrix (for any of their groups) - allows access
  • Otherwise - denies access (403 Forbidden)

docs.title: Levels
docs.text: This document outlines the API endpoints for viewing member levels (experience tiers).

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
Levels represent experience/seniority tiers in the club (e.g., Newbie, Intermediate, Explorer, Marshal). They determine which trips a member can join, which permissions they have, and when they are eligible for an upgrade.

Levels are managed by administrators via Django Admin. The API provides read-only access.

docs.title: Logbook Migration
docs.text: The logbook migration feature allows members who have purchased paper logbooks to migrate their existing signatures and skills to the digital system.

docs.title: Member-Initiated Migration
docs.text: Any member can submit a migration request to transfer skills from their physical logbook. Non-paid members can submit with empty skill entries to become paid members upon approval. Paid members must include skill entries to migrate their skills.

docs.title: Manager Direct Migration
docs.text: A trip manager (marshal with APPROVE_LOGBOOK_MIGRATION permission) can enter data directly for a member, bypassing the review cycle. The request is approved immediately upon creation.

docs.title: Create Migration Request
docs.text:
• POST /api/logbook-migrations/
  • Creates a new migration request.
  • Requires authentication.
  • Supports multipart/form-data for PDF upload.

docs.title: List Migration Requests
docs.text:
• GET /api/logbook-migrations/
  • Lists migration requests for the authenticated user.
  • Admins/marshals with APPROVE_LOGBOOK_MIGRATION permission see all requests.
  • Query parameters: status, migration_type, member, target_level

docs.title: Get Migration Request Details
docs.text:
• GET /api/logbook-migrations/{id}/
  • Retrieves details of a specific migration request.

docs.title: Approve Migration Request
docs.text:
• PATCH /api/logbook-migrations/{id}/approve/
  • Approves a pending migration request.
  • Requires APPROVE_LOGBOOK_MIGRATION permission.
  • Creates logbook entries and skill references on approval.
  • Sets member's paid_member to true if not already paid.

docs.title: Return Migration Request
docs.text:
• PATCH /api/logbook-migrations/{id}/return-request/
  • Returns a request to the member for amendments.
  • Requires APPROVE_LOGBOOK_MIGRATION permission.

docs.title: Reject Migration Request
docs.text:
• PATCH /api/logbook-migrations/{id}/reject/
  • Rejects a pending migration request.
  • Requires APPROVE_LOGBOOK_MIGRATION permission.

docs.title: Edit and Resubmit
docs.text:
• PUT /api/logbook-migrations/{id}/
  • Allows editing a returned request and resubmitting.
  • Only allowed when status is RETURNED.

docs.title: Permissions
docs.text: Action Who Create own request, view own requests Authenticated members View all requests, approve/return/reject Users with APPROVE_LOGBOOK_MIGRATION Create MANAGER_DIRECT requests Users with APPROVE_LOGBOOK_MIGRATION

docs.title: Status Transitions
docs.text:
• PENDING → APPROVED (admin approves)
  • PENDING → RETURNED (admin sends back)
  • PENDING → REJECTED (admin rejects)
  • RETURNED → PENDING (member edits and resubmits)

docs.title: Digital Logbook
docs.text: The digital logbook allows members to track their progress and have their skills verified by trip leads.

docs.title: Create a Logbook Entry
docs.text:
• POST /api/trips/{id}/logbook-entries

    Note: This endpoint does NOT use a trailing slash.

    • Creates a new logbook entry for a trip.
    • Requires CREATE_LOGBOOK_ENTRIES or CREATE_LOGBOOK_ENTRIES_SUPERUSER permission.

docs.title: View Logbook Entries for a Trip
docs.text:
• GET /api/trips/{id}/viewlogbooks

    Note: This endpoint does NOT use a trailing slash.

    • Retrieves a list of members checked in to a trip, along with their associated logbook entry.

docs.title: View Logbook Entries for a Member
docs.text:
• GET /api/members/{id}/logbookentries

    Note: This endpoint does NOT use a trailing slash.

    • Retrieves a list of logbook entries for a specific member.
    • Each entry includes created_at and updated_at timestamps for audit trail purposes.
    • When skills are verified, LogbookSkillReference records are created with signed_by, entered_by, and entered_at fields.

docs.title: List Logbook Skills
docs.text:
• GET /api/logbookskills/

    Note: This endpoint uses a trailing slash (it is a router-registered ViewSet endpoint).

    • Retrieves a list of all available logbook skills (only active skills, ordered by order field).
    • The count_requirement field indicates the minimum number of sign-offs required for a skill.
    • The category field is an object containing the ID and name of the skill category.
    • Pagination: Standard pagination (default 20, max 500).

Query Parameters:

Parameter Type Description category integer Filter by skill category ID level_gte integer Skills for levels with ID >= this value level_lte integer Skills for levels with ID <= this value level_eq integer Skills for an exact level ID level_null boolean Skills with no level requirement (true or false)

docs.title: Logbook Entries ViewSet (CRUD)
docs.text:
The following router-registered endpoints provide full CRUD access to logbook entries:

  • GET /api/logbookentries/ - List all logbook entries, ordered by ID.
  • GET /api/logbookentries/{id}/ - Retrieve a single entry.
  • POST /api/logbookentries/ - Create a new logbook entry (alternative to POST /api/trips/{id}/logbook-entries). Requires CREATE_LOGBOOK_ENTRIES permission. Body includes trip, member, comment, and skills_verified (array of skill IDs).
  • PUT/PATCH /api/logbookentries/{id}/ - Update an entry. Same permission checks as create.
  • DELETE /api/logbookentries/{id}/ - Delete an entry.

Note: Both the trip-specific endpoint (POST /api/trips/{id}/logbook-entries) and the ViewSet endpoint (POST /api/logbookentries/) can be used to create entries. They apply the same permission checks.

docs.title: Logbook Skill References ViewSet
docs.text:
• GET /api/logbookskillreferences/ - List all skill reference records.
  • GET /api/logbookskillreferences/{id}/ - Retrieve a single skill reference.
  • Full CRUD is available (POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE) for authenticated users with appropriate permissions.

Skill Reference Fields: id, logbook_skill, member, trip, signed_by, entered_by, entered_at

docs.title: Logbook Entry Permissions
docs.text: Creating, updating, and deleting logbook entries is governed by a detailed permission system. The rules are as follows:

docs.title: Members Creating Entries for Themselves
docs.text:
• A member cannot create, update, or delete a logbook entry for themselves.
  • Exception: A member with the CREATE_LOGBOOK_ENTRIES_SUPERUSER permission can create, update, or delete an entry for themselves, provided they are registered for the trip.

docs.title: Members Creating Entries for Other Members
docs.text:
• Trip Lead or Deputy Lead: A trip lead or deputy lead can create, update, or delete a logbook entry for another member, provided that the other member is registered for the trip. The lead/deputy lead does not need to be registered themselves.
  • Superuser (CREATE_LOGBOOK_ENTRIES_SUPERUSER): A member with this permission can create, update, or delete a logbook entry for another member, provided that the other member is registered for the trip.
  • Regular Member (with CREATE_LOGBOOK_ENTRIES permission): A regular member can create, update, or delete a logbook entry for another member if all of the following conditions are met:
  • The acting member is registered for the trip.
  • The other member is registered for the trip.
  • The acting member has the CREATE_LOGBOOK_ENTRIES permission that applies to the trip's level.

docs.title: Skill Sign-Off Validation (when skills_verified are included in the request)
docs.text:
A user can sign off on skills for another user if any of the following are true:

  • They are the Trip Lead or Deputy Lead for the associated trip.
  • They have the SIGN_LOGBOOK_SKILLS permission AND are registered for the associated trip themselves.
  • They have the CREATE_LOGBOOK_ENTRIES_SUPERUSER permission (this permission bypasses all other skill sign-off checks).

If a user has permission to create or update a logbook entry but lacks the required skill sign-off permissions, the entire request will be denied if it includes skills_verified.

docs.title: Auto-Upgrade on First Logbook Entry
docs.text: When enabled via Global Settings, members can be automatically upgraded to the next level after their first logbook entry is created.

docs.title: How It Works
docs.text:
1. A logbook entry is created for a member
  2. The system checks if:
  3. Auto-upgrade is enabled in global settings
  4. The member is at the configured source_level
  5. If conditions are met, the member is automatically upgraded to the target_level
  6. The member is also added to the target level's auto_group (if configured)

docs.title: Reverting Upgrade
docs.text: If a logbook entry is deleted and it was the member's only logbook entry, the upgrade is automatically reverted: 1. The system detects the deletion 2. Checks if the member has any remaining logbook entries 3. If no entries remain, the member is reverted to the source_level 4. The member is removed from the target level's auto_group (if different from source)

docs.title: Maintenance Mode
docs.text: AD4x4 supports a site-wide maintenance toggle that responds to every HTTP request with 503 Service Unavailable and a short HTML page. The feature is implemented at the nginx layer, not in Django — so it keeps working even if the Django app or Huey workers are being restarted, migrated, or are otherwise unavailable.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
The nginx container inside the Docker Compose stack checks for a marker file on every incoming request:

  • If /etc/nginx/maintenance/maintenance_on exists → nginx returns 503 Service Unavailable with a Retry-After: 3600 header and a small HTML body, regardless of the URL
  • If the file is absent → traffic flows through to Django and the static locations as normal

The marker directory (nginx/maintenance/) is mounted as a shared volume between the host and the nginx container in infra/docker-compose.yml, so creating or removing the marker from the host is immediately visible to nginx. The nginx if (-f ...) check is re-evaluated per request, so a config reload isn't strictly required for the state change to take effect — but both scripts run nginx -s reload anyway as a belt-and-braces measure so any in-flight keep-alive connections see a clean state.

The nginx block that implements the check lives in infra/nginx/secure/default.conf.template:

set $maintenance_mode 0;
if (-f /etc/nginx/maintenance/maintenance_on) {
    set $maintenance_mode 1;
}
if ($maintenance_mode = 1) {
    return 503;
}
error_page 503 @maintenance;
location @maintenance {
    default_type text/html;
    add_header Retry-After 3600;
    return 503 '<html><body><h1>Maintenance</h1><p>We'll be back soon.</p></body></html>';
}

Because the if blocks are at the server {} level and run before location routing, everything under the host — API endpoints, the Django admin, /static/, /uploads/, Swagger UI — is blocked in one sweep. There is no way to keep any path responding through nginx while maintenance mode is enabled.

docs.title: Enabling maintenance mode
docs.text:
From the production host, with shell access as admin:

cd /home/admin/ad4x4/infra
./enable_maintenance_mode.sh

The script creates the marker file and reloads nginx:

#!/bin/bash
touch ./nginx/maintenance/maintenance_on
docker exec nginx nginx -s reload

The site starts returning 503 immediately. Verify from another machine:

curl -I https://ap.ad4x4.com/
# HTTP/2 503
# retry-after: 3600

docs.title: Disabling maintenance mode
docs.text:
From the production host:

cd /home/admin/ad4x4/infra
./disable_maintenance_mode.sh

The script removes the marker file and reloads nginx:

#!/bin/bash
rm ./nginx/maintenance/maintenance_on
docker exec nginx nginx -s reload

Normal traffic resumes immediately.

docs.title: Why nginx instead of a Django middleware
docs.text:
Putting the maintenance gate at nginx rather than a Django middleware has two operational advantages:

  • Nothing in Django needs to be running. The 503 is served even if the Django container is stopped, the database is mid-migration, Huey is stuck, or a release has just unhealthy-checked out. Those are the exact scenarios where maintenance mode matters most.
  • No request ever reaches Django during maintenance, so there is no database load and no risk of side effects from partially processed requests.

The trade-off is that there is no way for API clients to negotiate a structured maintenance window — the body is a static HTML page, not a JSON envelope with Retry-After metadata or a message key. Clients should match on 503 + Retry-After header to detect the state.

docs.title: Client behaviour
docs.text:
The mobile app and web clients should treat 503 responses during any request as a transient maintenance state and:

  1. Show a "We'll be back soon" screen with a manual retry affordance.
  2. Back off for at least the duration in the Retry-After header (currently 3600 seconds).
  3. Do not send these to Sentry / error reporting — they are expected operational states, not bugs, and will drown real errors.

docs.title: Gotchas
docs.text:
• The marker file is on the production host, not in the Django database. There is no API endpoint to enable or disable maintenance mode. It's a deliberate ops-level action that requires shell access to the Hetzner host.
  • Static files under /static/ are also blocked during maintenance because the if check runs at the server {} level before location routing kicks in. This is intentional — we don't want the app UI to render half-loaded while the backend is unreachable.
  • There is no Django-level maintenance toggle. ConfigurableSettings does not have a maintenance_mode_enabled field, and there is no custom Django middleware for this purpose. Do not try to add one — the nginx-based flow is the authoritative mechanism, and a duplicate toggle would split-brain the state.
  • nginx -s reload is a belt-and-braces step. The if (-f ...) check is re-evaluated on every request even without reloading, but the reload guarantees all worker processes agree on the new state for in-flight keep-alive connections.
  • The Huey worker container is unaffected by maintenance mode — scheduled tasks and background notifications continue to run. If you need to stop Huey as well, that's a separate docker compose stop huey action.

docs.title: Meeting Points
docs.text: This document outlines the API endpoints for managing meeting points.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Meeting points are predefined locations where trip participants can gather. The API provides endpoints for creating, viewing, updating, and deleting these points.

docs.title: List Meeting Points
docs.text:
• GET /api/meetingpoints/
    • Retrieves a list of all available meeting points, ordered by name.
    • Caching: the response carries Cache-Control: public, max-age=600, so clients and intermediaries may cache the list for up to 10 minutes. If your UI must reflect a newly-created meeting point immediately, bypass the cache (e.g. with a cache-busting query param) or refetch after the TTL expires.

Query Parameters:

Parameter Type Description name string Filter by exact name name__icontains string Filter by name (case-insensitive partial match) area string Filter by area code (e.g., DXB, AUH, NOR, AAN, LIW)

docs.title: Retrieve a Meeting Point
docs.text:
• GET /api/meetingpoints/{id}/
    • Retrieves the details of a single meeting point.

docs.title: Create a Meeting Point
docs.text:
• POST /api/meetingpoints/
    • Creates a new meeting point. Requires the CREATE_MEETING_POINTS permission.
    • Request Body: json { "name": "Al Faya", "lat": 24.733, "lon": 55.766, "link": "https://goo.gl/maps/...", "area": "AUH" } Note: The area field can be one of DXB, NOR, AUH, AAN, or LIW.

docs.title: Update a Meeting Point
docs.text:
• PUT or PATCH /api/meetingpoints/{id}/
    • Updates an existing meeting point. Requires the EDIT_MEETING_POINTS permission.
    • The request body should contain the fields to be updated.

docs.title: Delete a Meeting Point
docs.text:
• DELETE /api/meetingpoints/{id}/
    • Deletes a meeting point. Requires the DELETE_MEETING_POINTS permission.

docs.title: Members
docs.text:
This document outlines the API endpoints for member management, including searching for members, retrieving member profiles, and managing member information.

For authentication and registration details, please refer to the Authentication and Profiles document.

docs.title: Member List
docs.text:
You can retrieve a list of members using the standard ViewSet endpoint.

GET /api/members/

Authentication: Optional (public endpoint, but contact info requires authentication and permissions)

Query Parameters:

Parameter Type Description trip_count integer Filter by exact trip count trip_count__range string Filter by trip count range (e.g., 5,20) phone string Filter by exact phone number phone__icontains string Filter by partial phone number level__numeric_level integer Filter by exact numeric level level__numeric_level__range string Filter by numeric level range level__name string Filter by exact level name level__name__icontains string Filter by partial level name email string Filter by exact email address email__icontains string Filter by partial email (contains) first_name string Filter by exact first name first_name__icontains string Filter by partial first name last_name string Filter by exact last name last_name__icontains string Filter by partial last name level__id integer Filter by level ID nationality string Filter by exact nationality code city string Filter by exact city paid_member boolean Filter by payment status (true or false) last_visited__isnull boolean Filter by visit status (true = never visited, false = visited at least once) last_visited_after datetime Filter members who last visited after this date/time (ISO 8601) last_visited_before datetime Filter members who last visited before this date/time (ISO 8601) date_joined_after date Filter members who joined after this date (e.g., 2026-03-01) date_joined_before date Filter members who joined before this date (e.g., 2026-04-01) search string Text search across username, first name, last name, and email (case-insensitive partial match). Optional — omitting returns all members. ordering string Sort results. Accepted values: username, first_name, last_name, trip_count, level__numeric_level, date_joined, id, last_visited. Prefix with - for descending (e.g., -trip_count). Multi-field: -trip_count,username. Default: id. page integer Page number (default: 1) page_size integer Number of results per page (default: 20, max: 500)

Note: Vehicle-related filters (car_brand, car_year) are NOT supported. Vehicle data is managed separately via the Vehicles endpoints.

Success Response:

{
  "count": 100,
  "next": "http://api.example.com/api/members/?page=2",
  "previous": null,
  "results": [
    {
      "id": 1,
      "username": "testuser",
      "firstName": "Test",
      "lastName": "User",
      "level": "Newbie",
      "tripCount": 5,
      "paidMember": true,
      "lastVisited": "2026-03-30T14:22:00Z"
    }
  ]
}

Note: In the list response, level is returned as a string (level name). In the detail response (/api/members/{id}/), level is a full object. Contact information (email, phone) is only visible to users with the VIEW_CONTACT_INFO permission or when viewing their own profile.

docs.title: Search Members
docs.text:
Search for members by username, first name, or last name. This is useful for finding members when adding trip participants, looking up member profiles, or searching for trip leads.

GET /api/members/search

Note: This endpoint does NOT use a trailing slash.

Authentication: Required (Bearer token)

Query Parameters:

Parameter Type Required Description query string Yes Search term - must be at least 3 characters. Matches against username, first name, and last name (case-insensitive partial match) level integer No Level ID for filtering to include only members at a specific level min_level integer No Minimum numeric level for filtering (inclusive) max_level integer No Maximum numeric level for filtering (inclusive) page integer No Page number (default: 1) page_size integer No Number of results per page (default: 20, max: 500)

Level Filtering Examples:

# Search for Newbies (level ID 10)
GET /api/members/search?query=john&level=10

# Search for members up to Intermediate (numeric level 100) inclusive
GET /api/members/search?query=john&max_level=100

# Search for members Intermediate (numeric level 100) and higher inclusive
GET /api/members/search?query=john&min_level=100

Request Example:

# Basic search
curl -X GET "http://localhost:8000/api/members/search?query=john&page=1&page_size=20" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <your-token>"

Success Response (200 OK):

{
  "count": 42,
  "next": "http://api.example.com/api/members/search?query=john&page=2",
  "previous": null,
  "results": [
    {
      "id": 1,
      "username": "johndoe",
      "firstName": "John",
      "lastName": "Doe",
      "level": "Marshal",
      "tripCount": 25,
      "paidMember": true,
      "lastVisited": "2026-03-30T14:22:00Z"
    }
  ]
}

Error Response (400 Bad Request - Missing query):

{
  "success": false,
  "message": "query_parameter_required"
}

Error Response (400 Bad Request - Query too short):

{
  "success": false,
  "message": "query_too_short"
}

Error Response (401 Unauthorized):

{
  "detail": "Authentication credentials were not provided."
}

Error Response (403 Forbidden):

{
  "detail": "You do not have permission to perform this action."
}

Notes: - The search is case-insensitive and performs partial matching (contains) - Query must be at least 3 characters long - Results are ordered by trip_count (descending), then by id (ascending) - Results are paginated using standard pagination - Matches across username, first_name, and last_name fields using OR logic - Results can be filtered by level using level, min_level, or max_level parameters - Contact information (email, phone) is only visible to users with the VIEW_CONTACT_INFO permission or when viewing their own profile - Permission Required: Users must have the SEARCH_MEMBERS permission to use this endpoint. By default, this is granted to Newbie level and above. ANIT members cannot use this endpoint.

docs.title: Member Trip History
docs.text:

Permissions: - Users can always view their own trip history. - To view another member's trip history, users need the VIEW_MEMBER_TRIP_HISTORY permission. - Superusers can view any member's trip history.

Response Fields:

Field Type Description id integer Trip ID title string Trip title description string Trip description startTime datetime Trip start time endTime datetime Trip end time lead object Trip lead {id, username} level object Level {id, name, numericLevel, minTripsForUpgrade, active, displayName} checkedIn boolean Whether the member is checked in for this trip image string/null Trip cover image URL meetingPoint object/null Meeting point {id, name, area, lat, lon, link} registeredCount integer Number of registered members capacity integer Trip capacity allowWaitlist boolean Whether the trip allows waitlisting approvalStatus string Approval status (A, P, C) isRegistered boolean Whether the target member is registered isWaitlisted boolean Whether the target member is on the waitlist

docs.text:

docs.text:
