docs.title: Member Payments
docs.text:
Manually update the paidMember field for a member.

POST /api/members/{id}/payments

Note: This endpoint does NOT use a trailing slash.

Authentication: Required (Bearer token)

Permission: Requires EDIT_MEMBERSHIP_PAYMENTS permission.

Request Body:

{
  "paymentReceived": "true"
}

Success Response:

{
  "success": true,
  "message": "payment_status_updated"
}

docs.title: Notifications
docs.text: This document outlines the different types of push and email notifications sent by the backend.

docs.title: Registering for Push Notifications
docs.text:
To receive push notifications, the client application must register the device's FCM token with the backend. This is done by making a POST request to the /api/device/fcm/ endpoint.

POST /api/device/fcm/

Request Body:

{
    "registrationId": "your-fcm-token",
    "type": "ios"
}

The type can be ios, android, or web.

For more information on Firebase Cloud Messaging, please refer to the official documentation.

docs.title: Trips
docs.text:
• New Trip Notification: Sent when a new trip is created.
  • Trip Approval Notification: Sent when a trip is approved or rejected.
  • Accepted from Waitlist: Sent to a member when they are moved from the waitlist to the registered list for a trip.
  • Removed from Trip Registered List: Sent to a member when they are removed from the registered list for a trip.
  • Removed from Trip Waitlist: Sent to a member when they are removed from the waitlist for a trip.
  • New Trip Comment: Sent when a new comment is added to a trip. This is a push-only notification and is NOT stored in the notification log.

docs.title: Upgrade Requests
docs.text:
• Upgrade Request Handled: Sent to a member when their upgrade request has been handled (approved or rejected).
  • Upgrade Request Created: Sent to the marshals when a new upgrade request is created.
  • Upgrade Request Reminder: A periodic reminder sent to the marshals about open upgrade requests.

docs.title: Club News
docs.text: • Club-Wide News: Sent to all members when a new club news item is published.

docs.title: Feedback
docs.text: • Feedback Notification: Sent to administrators when a member submits feedback via email/Telegram. This is not stored as a NotificationType log entry and does not appear in the notification history endpoint.

docs.title: NotificationType Enum Values
docs.text:
The type field in the notification object will contain one of the following enum values:

Value Description NEW_TRIP A new trip has been created. TRIP_APPR A trip has been approved or rejected. WAIT_ACC A user has been accepted from the waitlist. UPG_REQ_HAN An upgrade request has been handled. UPG_REQ_CRE A new upgrade request has been created. UPG_REQ_REM A reminder for an open upgrade request. CLUB_NEWS A new club news item has been published. REM_FROM_TRIP_REG A user has been removed from a trip's registered list. REM_FROM_TRIP_WAIT A user has been removed from a trip's waitlist.

Note: Trip comment notifications are sent via push only and do not appear in the notification log. There is no NEW_TRIP_COMMENT enum value in NotificationType.

docs.title: Notification History
docs.text:
A log of all notifications sent to a member is stored in the database. This allows the client application to display a history of notifications to the user.

GET /api/notifications/

Authentication: Required (Bearer token)

The endpoint returns the 20 most recent notifications for the authenticated user, ordered by timestamp descending.

Response Fields:

Field Type Description id integer Unique notification ID title string Notification title body string Notification body text timestamp datetime When the notification was created type string Notification type enum value (see table above) relatedObjectId integer ID of the related object (e.g., trip ID, upgrade request ID). Can be null. relatedObjectType string Type of the related object (e.g., "trip", "upgrade_request"). Can be null. isRead boolean Whether the notification has been read

Response Example:

[
  {
    "id": 1,
    "title": "Trip Approved",
    "body": "Your trip 'Desert Safari' has been approved.",
    "timestamp": "2026-03-15T10:00:00",
    "type": "TRIP_APPR",
    "relatedObjectId": 456,
    "relatedObjectType": "trip",
    "isRead": false
  }
]

Note: The endpoint returns a plain array of the 20 most recent notifications (no pagination wrapper). All field names use camelCase in the response.

docs.title: Marking Notifications as Read
docs.text:
To mark one or more notifications as read, the client can make a POST request to the /api/notifications/mark-as-read/ endpoint.

POST /api/notifications/mark-as-read/

Request Body:

{
    "notificationIds": [1, 2, 3]
}

The notificationIds field should contain a list of notification IDs to be marked as read. The endpoint will return a 204 No Content response on success.

Error Response (400 Bad Request):

{
    "detail": "notification_ids must be provided."
}

{
    "detail": "One or more notification IDs are invalid or do not belong to the user."
}

docs.title: Notification Settings
docs.text:
Members can configure their notification preferences.

GET /api/auth/profile/notificationsettings

Note: This endpoint does NOT use a trailing slash.

Authentication: Required (Bearer token)

Response:

{
  "clubNewsEnabledEmail": false,
  "clubNewsEnabledAppPush": true,
  "newTripAlertsEnabledEmail": false,
  "newTripAlertsEnabledAppPush": true,
  "newTripAlertsLevelFilter": [],
  "upgradeRequestReminderEmail": true,
  "tripChatEnabledAppPush": true,
  "lastUserActivity": "2026-03-15"
}

Fields:

Field Type Description clubNewsEnabledEmail boolean Receive club news via email clubNewsEnabledAppPush boolean Receive club news via push notification newTripAlertsEnabledEmail boolean Receive new trip alerts via email newTripAlertsEnabledAppPush boolean Receive new trip alerts via push notification newTripAlertsLevelFilter array Level IDs to filter trip alerts. Empty = all levels. upgradeRequestReminderEmail boolean Receive upgrade request reminders via email tripChatEnabledAppPush boolean Receive push notifications for trip chat messages lastUserActivity date Last user activity date (read-only, auto-updated). Note: This is a date-only field on the notification settings model. For datetime-precision activity tracking with filtering and ordering support, use the lastVisited field on the Member model — see Members.

PUT/PATCH /api/auth/profile/notificationsettings

Update notification settings. All fields except lastUserActivity are writable.

Request Body (example partial update):

{
  "clubNewsEnabledEmail": true,
  "newTripAlertsLevelFilter": [1, 2]
}

docs.title: Notification Purging
docs.text: To prevent the notification log from growing indefinitely, a periodic background task runs daily to purge old notifications. Any notification logs older than 60 days are automatically deleted from the database.

docs.title: Permissions, Groups, and Levels
docs.text: This document provides a comprehensive overview of the permissions system used in the API. It details the different user groups, experience levels, and the specific actions each group is permitted to perform by default.

docs.title: Core Concepts
docs.text:
The permissions system is built on three main concepts:

  • Groups: Users are assigned to one or more groups, which determine their general role and permissions.
  • Levels: Levels represent a user's experience or seniority within the club (e.g., Newbie, Intermediate, Marshal). Some permissions are restricted to certain levels.
  • Actions: These are specific permissions that grant the ability to perform a particular operation via the API (e.g., CREATE_TRIP, APPROVE_UPGRADE_REQ).

Permissions are granted to groups, and can optionally be restricted to apply only to certain levels.

docs.title: Fetching User Permissions
docs.text:
To get the permissions for a specific user, you can retrieve their profile from the /api/members/{id}/ endpoint. The user's permissions are included in the permissions array in the response.

GET /api/members/{id}/

Example Response Snippet:

{
    "id": 1,
    "username": "testuser",
    ...
    "permissions": [
        {"id": 1, "action": "create_trip", "levels": []},
        {"id": 2, "action": "view_contact_info", "levels": []}
    ],
    ...
}

Note: Each permission entry is an object, not a plain string. The action field contains the lowercase DB value (e.g., "create_trip", not "CREATE_TRIP"). The levels field is an array of level objects ({id, name, numericLevel, minTripsForUpgrade}) for level-restricted permissions, or an empty array for permissions that apply to all levels.

docs.title: Groups and Levels
docs.text:
The following table lists the default groups and their corresponding experience levels:

Group Level Numeric Level Notes Newbies Newbie 10 Default for new users Intermediates Intermediate 100 Advanced Advance 200 Experts Expert 300 Disabled by default Explorers Explorer 400 Marshals Marshal 600 Board members Board member 800 Non-level Groups Trip managers N/A N/A Meeting point managers N/A N/A Media managers N/A N/A Upgrade request managers N/A N/A Site admins N/A N/A Super-users with all permissions

docs.title: Default Permissions by Group
docs.text: Here is a breakdown of the default permissions assigned to each group.

docs.title: Newbies
docs.text: • Can search for members in the member directory.

docs.title: Explorers
docs.text:
• Can create trips that require approval for the "Newbie" level.
  • Can create trips that do not require approval for "Intermediate" level and above.
  • Can create meeting points.
  • Can view contact information of other members.
  • Can create logbook entries and sign off on skills for trips they lead or support

docs.title: Marshals
docs.text:
• Can create trips without requiring approval.
  • Can view, vote on, and comment on upgrade requests.

docs.title: Board Members
docs.text:
• Can view, vote on, and comment on upgrade requests.
  • Can approve upgrade requests.
  • Can override the global waitlist setting for trips.

docs.title: Upgrade Request Managers
docs.text:
• Can view, vote on, comment on, edit, and delete upgrade requests.
  • Can delete comments on upgrade requests.

docs.title: Trip Managers
docs.text:
• Can create, edit, approve, and delete trips.
  • Can edit trip registrations and delete trip comments.
  • Can override the global waitlist setting for trips.
  • Have superuser permissions for creating logbook entries.

docs.title: Media Managers
docs.text: • Can edit trip media.

docs.title: Meeting Point Managers
docs.text: • Can create, edit, and delete meeting points.

docs.title: Site Admins
docs.text: • Have all permissions.

docs.title: Full List of Permissions (Actions)
docs.text:
The following table lists all possible actions in the system. The Action (DB value) column shows the exact lowercase string returned by the API in the action field.

Note: Action values are all lowercase (e.g., "create_trip"). Two values differ from their enum names: OVERRIDE_WAITLIST_SETTING → "override_waitlist" and CREATE_UPGRADE_REQ_FOR_OTHERS → "create_upgrade_req_for_other" (singular).

Action (DB value) Description create_trip Create Trip create_trip_with_approval Create Trip With Approval create_trip_report Create Trip Report approve_trip Approve Trip override_waitlist Override Global Waitlist Setting bypass_level_req Bypass Level Requirements for Trip edit_trips Edit Trips edit_trip_media Edit Trip Media edit_trip_registrations Edit Trip Registrations delete_trips Delete Trips delete_trip_comments Delete Trip Comments create_meeting_points Create Meeting Points edit_meeting_points Edit Meeting Points delete_meeting_points Delete Meeting Points create_upgrade_req_for_self Create Upgrade Request For Self create_upgrade_req_for_other Create Upgrade Request For Others edit_upgrade_req Edit Upgrade Request approve_upgrade_req Approve Upgrade Request delete_upgrade_req Delete Upgrade Request view_upgrade_req View Upgrade Request (ALL levels) vote_upgrade_req Vote Upgrade Request create_comment_upgrade_req Comment Upgrade Request delete_comment_upgrade_req Delete Comment Upgrade Request edit_membership_payments Edit Membership Payments create_logbook_entries Create Logbook Entries sign_logbook_skills Sign Logbook Skills create_logbook_entries_superuser Create Logbook Entries (superuser bypass) approve_logbook_migration Approve Logbook Migration Requests access_marshal_panel Access Marshal Panel view_contact_info View Contact Info view_member_trip_history View Member Trip History search_members Search Members can_be_deputy_lead Can Be Deputy Lead edit_ui_strings Edit UI Strings edit_global_settings Edit Global Settings search_trips Search Trips view_trips_as_lead View Trips as Lead

docs.title: Groups API
docs.text: The Groups API provides read-only access to the list of user groups.

docs.title: List Groups
docs.text:
• GET /api/groups/
    • Retrieves a list of all groups, ordered by name.
    • Authentication: Optional (public for reading).

Example Response:

[
    {
        "id": 1,
        "name": "Board members",
        "permissions": [1, 5, 12]
    },
    {
        "id": 2,
        "name": "Explorers",
        "permissions": [3, 7, 8, 11]

]

docs.title: Retrieve a Group
docs.text:
• GET /api/groups/{id}/
    • Retrieves the details of a single group.

Note: Groups are managed via Django Admin. The API does not support creating, updating, or deleting groups.

docs.title: Permission Matrix API
docs.text: The Permission Matrix API provides read-only access to the mapping between groups, actions, and levels.

docs.title: List Permission Matrix Entries
docs.text:
• GET /api/permissionmatrix/
    • Retrieves a list of all permission matrix entries, ordered by ID.
    • Authentication: Optional (public for reading).

Example Response:

[
    {
        "id": 1,
        "action": "create_trip",
        "levels": [1, 2, 3],
        "group": 5
    },
    {
        "id": 2,
        "action": "approve_trip",
        "levels": [],
        "group": 7
    }
]
Field Type Description id integer Unique entry ID action string Permission action identifier (see actions table above) levels array List of Level IDs this permission applies to. Empty array means it applies to all levels. group integer Group ID this permission is assigned to

docs.title: Retrieve a Permission Matrix Entry
docs.text:
• GET /api/permissionmatrix/{id}/
    • Retrieves a single permission matrix entry.

Note: The permission matrix is managed via Django Admin. The API does not support creating, updating, or deleting entries.

docs.title: How Permission Checks Work
docs.text:
When the system checks if a user has a specific permission:

  1. It finds all PermissionMatrix entries where the action matches and the user belongs to the associated group.
  2. If the entry has no levels attached (empty array), the permission applies to all levels.
  3. If the entry has specific levels, the permission only applies when the target member/trip is at one of those levels.
  4. Superusers bypass all permission checks.

docs.title: Rate Limiting
docs.text: To ensure the stability and reliability of the AD4x4 API, we have implemented rate limiting at two levels: Nginx and Django REST Framework (DRF).

docs.title: Nginx Rate Limiting
docs.text: The rate limiting is configured in the Nginx default.conf.template file. The current limit is set to 100 requests per minute per IP address for most API endpoints, with stricter limits on registration endpoints.

docs.title: Django DRF Rate Limiting
docs.text:
The API also implements Django REST Framework throttling:

User Type Rate Anonymous users 100 requests/minute Authenticated users 200 requests/minute

docs.title: HTTP 429 Response
docs.text:
If you exceed the rate limit, the API will respond with an HTTP 429 Too Many Requests status code. When you receive this response, you should:

  • Stop sending requests: Do not send any more requests until the rate limit window has reset.
  • Inform the user: Display a message to the user indicating that they have exceeded the rate limit and should try again later.
  • Implement backoff: Consider implementing an exponential backoff strategy to gradually reduce the rate of your requests.

docs.title: Authorizing with a Bearer Token
docs.text:
To test the protected endpoints in the Swagger UI, you'll need to obtain a bearer token and authorize your requests. Here's how to do it:

  1. Obtain a JWT token: Send a POST request to /api/token/ with your username and password. The response contains an access token and a refresh token. Alternatively, /api/auth/login/ also returns a token (legacy rest_registration flow).

  2. Authorize in Swagger:

    • Click the "Authorize" button at the top-right of the Swagger page.
    • In the dialog that appears, enter the word Bearer followed by a space and then the access token you received in the previous step. For example: Bearer eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9...
    • Click "Authorize" to save the token.

Tokens are valid for 24 hours. Use /api/token/refresh/ to refresh an expired token without re-entering credentials.

Once you've authorized, you can make requests to any of the protected endpoints in the Swagger UI.

docs.title: Trip Search
docs.text: This document outlines the API endpoint for searching trips. For general trip management, please refer to the Trips document.

docs.title: Search Trips
docs.text:
Search for trips by title, with optional filters for level, date ranges, meeting point, and area. This endpoint is useful for finding specific trips, browsing trip history, or discovering trip activities.

Endpoint: GET /api/trips/search

Note: This endpoint does NOT use a trailing slash.

Authentication: Required (Bearer token) Permission Required: Users must have SEARCH_TRIPS permission to access this endpoint.

docs.title: Query Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Type Required Description query string No Search term - must be at least 3 characters if provided. Matches against trip title (case-insensitive partial match). At least one search parameter must be provided. level integer No Trip level ID for filtering to include only trips at a specific level min_level integer No Minimum level numeric value for filtering to include only trips at this level or higher (inclusive) max_level integer No Maximum level numeric value for filtering to include only trips at this level or lower (inclusive) start_date_min date (ISO 8601) No Filter for trips starting from this date (inclusive) start_date_max date (ISO 8601) No Filter for trips starting until this date (inclusive) end_date_min date (ISO 8601) No Filter for trips ending from this date (inclusive) end_date_max date (ISO 8601) No Filter for trips ending until this date (inclusive) meeting_point integer No Filter for trips at a specific meeting point (exact match by ID) area string No Filter for trips in a specific area (area code like DXB, AUH). Must be a string — numeric values are rejected. approval_status string No Filter by approval status. Accepted values: P (Pending), A (Approved), R (Rejected), C (Cancelled). Invalid values return 400. level_id integer No Filter by level database ID (e.g., 4 for Intermediate). This is an alternative to the level param which uses numericLevel values. ordering string No Sort results. Accepted values: start_time, -start_time, title, -title. Default: -start_time (newest first). Invalid values fall back to default. page integer No Page number (default: 1) page_size integer No Number of results per page (default: 20, max: 500)

docs.title: Request Examples
docs.text:
Basic search:

curl -X GET "http://api.example.com/api/trips/search?query=fun" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <your-token>"

Search with level filter:

curl -X GET "http://api.example.com/api/trips/search?query=adventure&level=10" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <your-token>"

Search with date range:

curl -X GET "http://api.example.com/api/trips/search?query=expedition&start_date_min=2026-01-01&end_date_max=2026-12-31" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <your-token>"

Search by meeting point:

curl -X GET "http://api.example.com/api/trips/search?query=beach&meeting_point=1" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <your-token>"

Search by area:

curl -X GET "http://api.example.com/api/trips/search?query=desert&area=DXB" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <your-token>"

Paginated search:

curl -X GET "http://api.example.com/api/trips/search?query=trip&page=1&page_size=10" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <your-token>"

Filter by approval status (approved only):

curl -X GET "http://api.example.com/api/trips/search?query=desert&approval_status=A" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <your-token>"

Sort by oldest first:

curl -X GET "http://api.example.com/api/trips/search?query=desert&ordering=start_time" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <your-token>"

Filter by level database ID:

curl -X GET "http://api.example.com/api/trips/search?query=desert&level_id=4" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <your-token>"

Combined filters (approved + oldest first + specific level):

curl -X GET "http://api.example.com/api/trips/search?query=desert&approval_status=A&ordering=start_time&level_id=4" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <your-token>"

docs.title: Error Responses
docs.text:
Error Response (400 Bad Request - No search parameters):

{
  "success": false,
  "message": "no_search_parameters_provided"
}

Error Response (400 Bad Request - Query too short):

{
  "success": false,
  "message": "query_too_short"
}

Error Response (400 Bad Request - Invalid integer parameter):

The level, min_level, max_level, and meeting_point parameters must be valid integers. If a non-numeric value is provided, the API returns:

{
  "success": false,
  "message": "invalid_level"
}
Parameter Error message level invalid_level min_level invalid_min_level max_level invalid_max_level meeting_point invalid_meeting_point_id

Error Response (400 Bad Request - Invalid area format):

The area parameter must be a string area code (e.g., DXB, AUH). Numeric values are rejected:

{
  "success": false,
  "message": "invalid_area_format"
}

Error Response (403 Forbidden):

{
  "detail": "You do not have permission to perform this action."
}

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• The search is case-insensitive and performs partial matching (contains) on trip titles
  • Query must be at least 3 characters long
  • Results are ordered by start_time (descending), then by id (ascending)
  • Results are paginated using standard pagination (20 items per page by default)
  • Level filtering: Use level for exact level match, or min_level/max_level for range filtering
  • Example: ?level=10 returns only Newbie trips
  • Example: ?min_level=100 returns Intermediate and higher level trips
  • Example: ?max_level=100 returns Newbie and Intermediate level trips
  • Date filtering: Use start_date_min/max and end_date_min/max to filter by date ranges
  • Trips that have ended (cut_off is in the past) are automatically excluded from results
  • If end_date_max is set without end_date_min, only trips ending on or before that date are included
  • Similarly for start dates
  • Meeting point filtering: Use meeting_point to filter by exact meeting point ID
  • Area filtering: Use area to filter by meeting point area code (e.g., DXB, AUH, AAN, NOR, LIW)
  • Approval status filter: Use approval_status to filter by status (P, A, R, C). Without this parameter, all statuses are returned.
  • Permission Required: Users must have SEARCH_TRIPS permission. By default, this is granted to Newbie level and above.
  • Performance Note: This endpoint searches trip titles efficiently. Searching by trip lead's user info (username, first name, last name) requires additional database joins and can be slower with many trips. Use title-based search for better performance.
  • User-specific information: For authenticated users, the response includes trip-specific registration status:
  • isRegistered: Whether the authenticated user is registered for this trip
  • isWaitlisted: Whether the authenticated user is on the waitlist for this trip
  • waitlistCount: Current number of users on the waitlist
  • registeredCount: Current number of users registered for this trip

docs.title: Use Cases
docs.text:
• Finding specific trips by title search
  • Browsing available trips for a specific level (e.g., Newbie trips only)
  • Discovering trip activities by date range
  • Finding trips at specific meeting points
  • Exploring trips in specific geographic areas
  • Checking trip history for a user or level
  • Building trip calendars or schedules

docs.title: Trips
docs.text: This document outlines the API endpoints for managing trips, including creating, viewing, registering, and managing participants.

docs.title: Trip Lifecycle
docs.text:
1. Creation: A trip is created via a POST request. Depending on the creator's permissions, it may be automatically approved or require manual approval.
  2. Approval: Trips requiring approval must be approved by a user with the appropriate permissions before they become visible to regular members.
  3. Registration: Once a trip is approved, members can register for it until the cut_off time is reached or the capacity is filled.
  4. Waitlist: If a trip is full and allow_waitlist is enabled, members can join the waitlist. They can optionally specify a vehicle when joining. The vehicle is stored and used when moved to registered. Members will be automatically moved to the registered list if a spot becomes available.
  5. Check-in/Check-out: The trip lead or a deputy can check members in and out of the trip.

docs.title: List and Retrieve Trips
docs.text:
• GET /api/trips/

    • Retrieves a list of all approved trips.

    • Query Parameters:

      Parameter Type Description lead integer Filter by trip lead (member ID) deputy_leads integer Filter by deputy lead (member ID) meeting_point integer Filter by meeting point ID meeting_point__area string Filter by meeting point area code (e.g., DXB, AUH) level__id integer Filter by level ID level__numeric_level integer Filter by exact numeric level level__numeric_level__range string Filter by numeric level range (e.g., 100,500) approval_status string Filter by approval status (A=Approved, P=Pending, R=Rejected, C=Cancelled) start_time_after datetime Filter trips starting after this date start_time_before datetime Filter trips starting before this date end_time_after datetime Filter trips ending after this date end_time_before datetime Filter trips ending before this date registered boolean Filter to only trips where the authenticated user is registered (true) or not registered (false). Requires authentication. waitlisted boolean Filter to only trips where the authenticated user is on the waitlist (true) or not waitlisted (false). Requires authentication. page integer Page number (default: 1) page_size integer Number of results per page (default: 20)

    Note: Both camelCase and snake_case parameter names are accepted (e.g., approvalStatus and approval_status are equivalent, startTimeAfter and start_time_after are equivalent).

  • GET /api/trips/{id}/

    • Retrieves the full details of a single trip, including registered members and the waitlist.
    • Contact Info: The trip lead and deputy leads' contact info (email, phone) is always visible to authenticated users. Other members' contact info requires VIEW_CONTACT_INFO permission.

docs.title: Create a Trip
docs.text:
• POST /api/trips

    Note: The create endpoint does NOT use a trailing slash. This differs from the list/retrieve endpoints which are router-registered.

    • Creates a new trip. The approval_status will be set based on the user's permissions.
    • Request Body: See the CreateTripSerializer for details. Key fields include:
      • lead (Member ID)
      • level (Level ID)
      • title
      • start_time
      • end_time
      • cut_off
      • capacity
      • meeting_point (MeetingPoint ID)

    Note: While the serializer and database use snake_case for field names (e.g., start_time), the API expects camelCase in the request body (e.g., startTime).

docs.title: Update a Trip
docs.text:
• PUT or PATCH /api/trips/{id}

    Note: The update/delete endpoint does NOT use a trailing slash.

    • Updates an existing trip.
    • Restrictions:
      • A configurable cutoff time (in minutes before the trip's start_time) determines when editing is restricted. The default is 0 minutes, meaning editing is disabled once the trip starts.
      • Before the cutoff time: The trip's lead and users with the EDIT_TRIPS permission can edit the trip.
      • After the cutoff time: Only users with the EDIT_TRIPS permission can edit the trip.
      • Superusers are exempt from all restrictions.
    • Request Body: See the UpdateTripSerializer for a list of editable fields.

docs.title: Delete a Trip
docs.text:
• DELETE /api/trips/{id}
    • Deletes a trip. This is a soft-delete, meaning the trip's approval_status is set to CANCELED.
    • Restrictions:
      • A configurable cutoff time (in minutes before the trip's start_time) determines when deleting is restricted. The default is 0 minutes, meaning deleting is disabled once the trip starts.
      • Before the cutoff time: The trip's lead and users with the DELETE_TRIPS permission can delete the trip.
      • After the cutoff time: Only users with the DELETE_TRIPS permission can delete the trip.
      • Superusers are exempt from all restrictions.

docs.title: Approve a Trip
docs.text:
• POST /api/trips/{id}/approve

    Note: This endpoint does NOT use a trailing slash.

    • Approves a trip that is pending approval. Requires the APPROVE_TRIP permission.
    • Side effects on the approver:
      1. The approver is added to the trip's deputy_leads.
      2. The approver is automatically registered as a participant (via add_to_registered()) using the provided vehicle_id, or their primary vehicle if none is given.
      3. The approver's TripRegistration.checked_in is set to true immediately (so they don't need to check themselves in on the day).
      4. send_trip_approval_notification and send_trip_notification are dispatched to Huey.
    • Request Body: {"vehicle_id": <vehicle_id>} (optional — defaults to the approver's primary vehicle)

docs.title: Decline a Trip
docs.text:
• POST /api/trips/{id}/decline

    Note: This endpoint does NOT use a trailing slash.

    • Declines a trip that is pending approval. Requires the APPROVE_TRIP permission.
    • Sets the trip's approval_status to REJECTED.
    • Triggers a trip approval notification.
    • Request Body: None required.
    • Success Response: {"success": true, "message": "trip_rejected"}

docs.title: Registration
docs.text:
Note: All registration endpoints below do NOT use trailing slashes.

  • POST /api/trips/{id}/register
    • Registers the authenticated user for the trip.
    • Request Body: {"vehicle_id": <vehicle_id>}
    • Required for regular users: Users must have at least one vehicle registered. Staff users (with EDIT_TRIP_REGISTRATIONS permission) can omit - defaults to their primary vehicle.
    • Returns vehicle_required error if no vehicle is provided.
    • Returns vehicle_not_found error if the vehicle doesn't exist or doesn't belong to the user.
    • Additional validations: trip_not_approved, level_insufficient, trip_cutoff_exceeded, trip_already_registered, trip_full.
    • Success Response: Returns the updated trip object alongside the success message: json {"success": true, "message": "trip_registered", "trip": { ...full trip object... }} The trip field contains the complete trip object (same schema as GET /api/trips/{id}/ list response) with updated registeredCount, isRegistered, isWaitlisted, etc. This eliminates the need for a follow-up GET request.
  • POST /api/trips/{id}/waitlist
    • Adds the authenticated user to the waitlist if the trip is full.
    • Request Body: {"vehicle_id": <vehicle_id>} (optional - defaults to user's primary vehicle)
    • Returns trip_waitlist_disabled_for_this_trip if waitlist is not enabled.
    • Success Response: {"success": true, "message": "trip_waitlisted", "trip": { ...full trip object... }}
  • POST /api/trips/{id}/unregister
    • Cancels the authenticated user's registration for the trip (from either the registered list or the waitlist).
    • Trip leads cannot unregister themselves (trip_lead_cannot_unregister).
    • Success Response: {"success": true, "message": "trip_registration_cancelled", "trip": { ...full trip object... }}

docs.title: Force Registration
docs.text:
• POST /api/trips/{id}/forceregister

    Note: This endpoint does NOT use a trailing slash.

    • Force-registers a member for a trip, bypassing level requirements and capacity checks. Requires BYPASS_LEVEL_REQ permission.
    • Request Body: json { "member": 123, "vehicle_id": 45 }
    • vehicle_id is optional; defaults to the member's primary vehicle.

docs.title: Participant Management
docs.text:
Note: All participant management endpoints below do NOT use trailing slashes.

  • POST /api/trips/{id}/addfromwaitlist
    • Manually moves a member from the waitlist to the registered list. Requires EDIT_TRIP_REGISTRATIONS permission or being the trip lead/deputy.
    • Request Body: {"member": <member_id>}
    • Success Response: {"success": true, "message": "member_moved_from_waitlist_to_registered"}
  • POST /api/trips/{id}/removemember
    • Removes a member from the trip (from either the registered list or the waitlist). Requires EDIT_TRIP_REGISTRATIONS permission or being the trip lead/deputy.
    • Request Body: {"member": <member_id>, "reason": "..."}
    • Success Response: {"success": true, "message": "user_removed_from_trip_registered"} or "user_removed_from_trip_waitlist"
  • POST /api/trips/{id}/checkin
    • Checks in one or more members to the trip. Requires EDIT_TRIP_REGISTRATIONS permission or being the trip lead/deputy.
    • Request Body: {"members": [<member_id_1>, <member_id_2>]}
  • POST /api/trips/{id}/checkout
    • Checks out one or more members from the trip. Requires EDIT_TRIP_REGISTRATIONS permission or being the trip lead/deputy.
    • Request Body: {"members": [<member_id_1>, <member_id_2>]}

Important: The checkin/checkout endpoints use a different response format from other trip endpoints:

json { "succeeded": [1, 2, 3], "failed": [ {"member": 4, "error": "Member is not registered for this trip"} ] }

This is NOT wrapped in the standard {"success": ..., "message": ...} format.

docs.title: Trip Comments
docs.text:
• GET /api/trips/{id}/comments

    Note: This endpoint does NOT use a trailing slash.

    • Retrieves comments for a specific trip, ordered by most recent first.
    • Authentication: Required.
    • Supports ordering via ordering query parameter (field: created).

    Response item fields: comment, member (object with id, username, displayName), trip, created

  • GET/POST/DELETE /api/tripcomments/

    This is the router-registered ViewSet for trip comments (uses trailing slash).

    • GET /api/tripcomments/ - List all comments. Filter by trip or member query params.
    • POST /api/tripcomments/ - Create a comment. Body: {"comment": "...", "trip": <trip_id>}. The member field is automatically set to the authenticated user.
    • DELETE /api/tripcomments/{id}/ - Delete a comment. Requires ownership or DELETE_TRIP_COMMENTS permission.

docs.title: Trip Reports (per trip)
docs.text:
• GET /api/trips/{id}/tripreports

    Note: This endpoint does NOT use a trailing slash.

    • Retrieves trip reports for a specific trip, ordered by ID.
    • Authentication: Required.

    See Trip Reports for the full CRUD Trip Reports API.

docs.title: Export Registrants
docs.text:
• GET /api/trips/{id}/exportregistrants

    Note: This endpoint does NOT use a trailing slash.

    • Exports the trip's registered members as a CSV file.
    • Authentication: Required.
    • Response: CSV file with Content-Disposition: attachment; filename="trip_{id}_registrants.csv"
    • CSV Columns: username, name, level, one column per active level for trip counts (e.g., trips_newbie, trips_intermediate), car_brand_model_color, phone, city

docs.title: View Logbooks
docs.text:
• GET /api/trips/{id}/viewlogbooks

    Note: This endpoint does NOT use a trailing slash.

    • Returns a list of checked-in members for the trip along with their logbook entry (if one exists).
    • Authentication: Required.
    • Each item in the response contains a member object and a logbook_entry object (or null).

    See Digital Logbook for the full logbook API.

docs.title: Member-Specific Trip Endpoints
docs.text:
These endpoints provide trip information tailored to a specific member.

Note: All member-specific endpoints below do NOT use trailing slashes.

docs.title: Member Trip Counts
docs.text:
• GET /api/members/{id}/tripcounts
    • Retrieves a summary of a member's completed trips, grouped by trip level.
    • Includes trips where the member was:
      • Registered and checked in (as participant)
      • Lead of the trip
      • Deputy lead of the trip
    • Only includes trips with an APPROVED status.
    • Trips are counted once even if member has multiple roles (lead + registered).

docs.title: Member Trip History
docs.text:
• GET /api/members/{id}/triphistory
    • Retrieves a paginated history of a member's trips.
    • Query Parameters: checked_in (boolean, filter for checked-in trips only), start_time (datetime filter).
    • Permissions: Own history always viewable. Viewing another member's history requires VIEW_MEMBER_TRIP_HISTORY permission or superuser.

    • Note: This endpoint only includes trips with an APPROVED status.

See also the Digital Logbook page for information on how to manage logbook entries for a trip.

docs.title: Upgrade Requests
docs.text: This document outlines the API endpoints for managing level upgrade requests.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Members can request to be upgraded to a higher level. This process involves creating a request, which is then reviewed and voted on by authorized members (e.g., Marshals, Board Members).

docs.title: List and Retrieve Upgrade Requests
docs.text:
• GET /api/upgraderequests/
    • Retrieves a list of upgrade requests. Requires VIEW_UPGRADE_REQ permission.
  • GET /api/upgraderequests/{id}/
    • Retrieves the details of a single upgrade request.

Voter fields — integer counts, not arrays: On both list and detail responses, yesVoters, noVoters, and deferVoters are returned as integer counts (the total number of members who voted yes/no/defer), not as arrays of member objects. nominatedVoters, however, IS returned as an array of member objects (the members who were nominated to vote on this request). Do not attempt to iterate yesVoters — use it as a number.

Status transitions: A request starts at status=N (NEW). When the first vote is cast it transitions to I (IN_PROGRESS). Final decisions set it to A (APPROVED) or D (DECLINED). verdictDate is auto-populated when status moves to APPROVED or DECLINED.

docs.title: Get Member Upgrade Eligibility
docs.text:
• GET /api/members/{id}/upgradeeligibility

    Note: This endpoint does NOT use a trailing slash.

    • Retrieves a detailed report on a member's eligibility for an upgrade to the next potential level. This report includes a breakdown of met/unmet requirements based on minimum trips at the current level and required logbook skills for the next level.
    • Authorization:
      • A member can view their own eligibility (when {id} matches request.user.id).
      • Members with the VIEW_UPGRADE_REQ permission can view the eligibility of any member.
      • Superusers can view any member's eligibility.

    • Response Structure (Example):

      Note: The backend builds the response in snake_case, but the camelCase middleware automatically converts the keys. The response you receive will use camelCase.

      json { "memberId": 1, "memberUsername": "testuser", "currentLevel": { "id": 1, "name": "Newbie", "numericLevel": 10 }, "nextPotentialLevel": { "id": 2, "name": "Intermediate", "numericLevel": 100 }, "upgradeRequirements": [ { "type": "min_trips", "name": "Minimum trips for current level", "requiredValue": 5, "currentValue": 3, "met": false, "description": "You need 5 trips at your current level (completed at this level).", "recentTripsAtLevel": [ { "tripId": 10, "title": "Desert Crossing", "startTime": "2026-01-15T09:00:00+04:00", "lead": {"id": 1, "username": "leader1"}, "level": {"id": 1, "name": "Newbie", "numericLevel": 10} }, { "tripId": 9, "title": "Mountain Trail", "startTime": "2025-12-20T08:00:00+04:00", "lead": {"id": 2, "username": "leader2"}, "level": {"id": 1, "name": "Newbie", "numericLevel": 10} } ] }, { "type": "logbook_skill", "skillId": 101, "skillName": "Basic Recovery", "requiredCount": 2, "currentCount": 1, "met": false, "description": "Complete 'Basic Recovery' 2 times.", "signatures": [ { "tripId": 15, "signedBy": {"id": 5, "username": "verifier_user"}, "signedDate": "2026-02-01T10:30:00+04:00" } ] }, { "type": "logbook_skill", "skillId": 102, "skillName": "Tyre Changing", "requiredCount": 1, "currentCount": 1, "met": true, "description": "Complete 'Tyre Changing' 1 time.", "signatures": [ { "tripId": 12, "signedBy": {"id": 6, "username": "another_verifier"}, "signedDate": "2026-01-25T14:00:00+04:00" } ] } ], "isEligibleForUpgrade": false }

docs.title: Create an Upgrade Request
docs.text:
• POST /api/upgraderequests/

    • Creates a new upgrade request.
    • Eligibility Check: Before creation, the system checks if the applicant is eligible for an upgrade based on minimum trips at their current level and required logbook skills for the target level. If the applicant is not eligible, or is already at the highest available level, the request will be rejected with a 400 Bad Request status and a detailed error message listing unmet requirements.
    • Request Body: See the CreateUpgradeRequestSerializer for details. Key fields include:
      • applicant (Member ID of the person being nominated for upgrade)
      • target_level (Level ID)
      • applicant_reason (Text description)
      • nominated_voters (List of Member IDs)

    Note: While the serializer and database use snake_case for field names (e.g., target_level), the API expects camelCase in the request body (e.g., targetLevel).

docs.title: Update an Upgrade Request
docs.text:
• PUT or PATCH /api/upgraderequests/{id}/
    • Updates an existing upgrade request. Requires EDIT_UPGRADE_REQ permission.

docs.title: Voting and Approval
docs.text:
• POST /api/upgraderequests/{id}/vote

    Note: This endpoint does NOT use a trailing slash.

    • Casts a vote on an upgrade request. Requires VOTE_UPGRADE_REQ permission.
    • Request Body: {"vote": "Y"} (or "N" for No, "D" for Defer)
    • Success Response: {"success": true, "message": "vote_accepted"}
    • Error: Returns upgrade_request_not_open_for_votes if the request status is not NEW or IN_PROGRESS. Returns invalid_vote_choice:<value> for unrecognized vote values.
    • Note: The first vote on a NEW request automatically moves its status to IN_PROGRESS.
    • POST /api/upgraderequests/{id}/approve/
    • Approves an upgrade request. Requires APPROVE_UPGRADE_REQ permission.
    • POST /api/upgraderequests/{id}/decline/
    • Declines an upgrade request. Requires APPROVE_UPGRADE_REQ permission.
    • Request Body: {"verdict_reason": "..."}

docs.title: Comments
docs.text:
• GET /api/upgraderequests/{id}/comments/
    • Retrieves all comments for a specific upgrade request.
  • POST /api/upgraderequestcomments/
    • Adds a new comment to an upgrade request. Requires CREATE_COMMENT_UPGRADE_REQ permission.
    • Request Body: {"upgrade_request": <request_id>, "text": "..."}
  • DELETE /api/upgraderequestcomments/{id}/
    • Deletes a comment. Requires DELETE_COMMENT_UPGRADE_REQ permission.

docs.title: Recently Approved Requests
docs.text:
• GET /api/upgraderequests/latestapproved

    Note: This endpoint does NOT use a trailing slash.

    • Retrieves a paginated list of recently approved upgrade requests, ordered by verdict date (most recent first).
    • Authentication: Not required (public endpoint).
    • Pagination: Standard pagination (default 20, max 500).

docs.title: Voted Requests
docs.text:
• GET /api/upgraderequests/voted

    Note: This endpoint does NOT use a trailing slash.

    • Returns an array of upgrade request IDs that the current user has voted on. Only includes requests with status NEW or IN_PROGRESS.
    • Authentication: Required.
    • Response: A plain array of integers, e.g., [1, 5, 12, 23]

  • GET /api/upgraderequests/{id}/voted

    Note: This endpoint does NOT use a trailing slash.

    • Checks whether the current user has voted on a specific upgrade request.
    • Authentication: Required.
    • Response: json { "success": true, "message": { "voted": true } }

docs.title: Global Settings

The vehicle limit per member can be configured in global settings:

docs.title: Trip Registration with Vehicle
docs.text: When registering for a trip, members must select which vehicle they will use. The vehicle information is stored with the trip registration and displayed in the trip details and export.

docs.title: Endpoints That Support Vehicle Registration
docs.text:
The following endpoints support optional vehicle_id parameter for vehicle association:

Endpoint Description Vehicle Source POST /api/trips/ Create trip (lead registered) Optional; defaults to lead's primary POST /api/trips/{id}/register/ User registers for trip Required for regular users; optional for staff POST /api/trips/{id}/forceregister Staff force-register a member Optional; defaults to member's primary POST /api/trips/{id}/approve/ Approve trip (approver registered) Optional; defaults to approver's primary POST /api/trips/{id}/waitlist Join waitlist Optional; stored with waitlist entry POST /api/trips/{id}/addfromwaitlist Move member from waitlist to registered Uses vehicle from waitlist entry

docs.title: Register for Trip
docs.text:
POST /api/trips/{tripId}/register

Authentication: Required (Bearer token)

Request Body:

{
  "vehicle_id": 123
}

Fields: | Field | Type | Required | Description | |-------|------|----------|-------------| | vehicle_id | integer | Yes* | ID of the vehicle to register with |

*Required for regular users. Users with edit_trip_registrations permission (staff/marshals) can omit - defaults to their primary vehicle.

Validation: - User must have at least one vehicle registered (unless staff with permission) - Vehicle must belong to the user - Vehicle is required (returns 400 error if not provided)

Success Response:

{
  "success": true,
  "message": "trip_registered"
}

Error Responses:

No vehicles registered:

{
  "success": false,
  "message": "vehicle_required"
}

Vehicle not found or doesn't belong to user:

{
  "success": false,
  "message": "vehicle_not_found"
}

POST /api/trips/

Vehicle Field: | Field | Type | Required | Description | |-------|------|----------|-------------| | vehicle_id | integer | No | ID of the vehicle the lead will use. Defaults to lead's primary vehicle if not specified. |

docs.text:
When a marshal approves a trip, they are automatically registered as a deputy lead.

Authentication: Required (Bearer token)

docs.text:
Members can join a trip waitlist and optionally specify their vehicle.

POST /api/trips/{tripId}/waitlist

Note: This endpoint does NOT use a trailing slash.

Authentication: Required (Bearer token)

Request Body:

{

docs.title: #1 — Add server-side filtering for user's registered/waitlisted trips
docs.text: Priority: High Endpoint: GET /api/trips/ Reported: Session #13 (2026-03-30)

docs.title: Problem
docs.text:
The My Trips portal page needs to show only trips where the logged-in user is registered or waitlisted. The API currently has no server-side filter for this. The frontend is forced to:

  1. Fetch ALL club trips (pageSize=100) — returns trips for every member, not just the requesting user
  2. Filter client-side using the isRegistered / isWaitlisted booleans on each trip object

This causes:

  • ~17-30 second load times on mobile (95 KB payload, 3,305 total trips in the database, only ~17 belong to the user out of the 100 returned)
  • Incomplete data — the Past tab can only show the user's trips that happen to fall within the most recent 100 trips. Older registered trips are invisible.
  • Wasted bandwidth — 80-95% of the downloaded data is discarded

docs.title: Evidence (tested 2026-03-30 with user Elle, ID 21144)
docs.text:
What we fetch Time Payload User's trips in response GET /api/trips/?startTimeBefore=2026-03-30&pageSize=100 ~1.5-17s 87-95 KB 17 out of 100 results GET /api/trips/?startTimeAfter=2026-03-30&pageSize=100 ~0.5s 7 KB 2 out of 5 results GET /api/members/21144/triphistory?pageSize=100 ~0.5s 4.6 KB 7 out of 7 (all user's)

We confirmed that registered=true and isRegistered=true query params are silently ignored — the count does not change.

docs.title: Recommended backend changes
docs.text:
Option A (preferred): Add query filters to GET /api/trips/

Add support for these query parameters:

GET /api/trips/?registered=true        -> only trips where the authenticated user is registered
GET /api/trips/?waitlisted=true        -> only trips where the authenticated user is waitlisted

The data already exists — the API already computes isRegistered and isWaitlisted per-trip in the response. This just needs to be wired up as a queryset filter. This would reduce the Past tab response from 3,305 trips to ~17, and from 95 KB to ~15 KB.

Option B (alternative): Enrich GET /api/members/{id}/triphistory

The triphistory endpoint already returns only the user's trips and is fast (0.5s, 4.6 KB). However, it returns a slim object missing several fields the portal needs:

Currently returned: id, title, description, startTime, endTime, lead, level, checkedIn

Missing fields needed by the portal: - image (trip cover photo URL) - meetingPoint (name, lat/lon, link, area) - registeredCount / capacity (registration count vs capacity) - isRegistered / isWaitlisted (registration status badges) - allowWaitlist (UI logic for full-trip warnings) - approvalStatus (filter cancelled/rejected trips)

Adding these fields to the triphistory response would make it a drop-in replacement.

docs.title: Why not fetch individual trip details?
docs.text: We tested GET /api/trips/{id}/ for each trip ID from triphistory. Each call takes 3-13 seconds. Seven sequential calls = ~90s. Even in parallel = ~21s. This is worse than the current approach.

docs.title: Frontend Audit Notes (from backend docs review — 2026-03-30)
docs.text: Confirmed still needed. Backend docs (trips.md, members.md) confirm: - GET /api/trips/ has NO registered or waitlisted filter parameter. - GET /api/members/{id}/triphistory returns slim objects missing: image, meetingPoint, registeredCount, capacity, isRegistered, isWaitlisted, allowWaitlist, approvalStatus. - New finding from vehicles.md: Trip registration responses now include a vehicle object. The triphistory endpoint is also missing this field. If Option B is chosen, vehicle should be added to the enriched response too. - All assumptions in our Problem section are valid.

docs.title: Implementation Record
docs.text:
Status: ✅ Complete (both options implemented — confirmed by backend team 2026-04-01)

What was changed: Backend team implemented BOTH Option A and Option B: - Option A: Added registered and waitlisted boolean query parameters to GET /api/trips/ - Option B: Enriched GET /api/members/{id}/triphistory with 9 additional fields (image, meetingPoint, registeredCount, capacity, isRegistered, isWaitlisted, allowWaitlist, approvalStatus, plus level as full object)

New/updated endpoint syntax (Option A):

Parameter Type Description registered boolean true = only trips where auth'd user is registered; false = only trips where NOT registered waitlisted boolean true = only trips where auth'd user is on waitlist; false = only trips where NOT waitlisted

These filters combine with all existing filters. Uses efficient Exists() subqueries.

Example request & response (Option A):

# Upcoming registered trips
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" \
  "https://ap.ad4x4.com/api/trips/?registered=true&startTimeAfter=2026-04-01&ordering=start_time"

# Past registered trips
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" \
  "https://ap.ad4x4.com/api/trips/?registered=true&startTimeBefore=2026-04-01&ordering=-start_time"

Expected impact: response size drops from ~3,305 trips (95 KB) to ~15-20 trips (~15 KB). Load time from 17-30s to <1s.

New/updated response fields (Option B — triphistory): Fields increased from 8 to 17: id, title, description, startTime, endTime, lead (object, serialized with ConciseMemberSerializer — returns only id and username), level (full object), checkedIn, image, meetingPoint (object), registeredCount, capacity, isRegistered, isWaitlisted, allowWaitlist, approvalStatus

Breaking changes: None — new fields are additive. Existing integrations unaffected.

Notes for frontend: - Use Option A for the "My Trips" portal page (registered/waitlisted tabs) - Use Option B for admin viewing of other members' trip history - Both filters require authentication. Unauthenticated requests ignore the filter. - registered=true and waitlisted=true can be combined (returns empty set since a user can't be both) - Default if neither is set: returns all trips (existing behaviour) - Ordering (ordering=start_time etc.) works alongside the new filters - See updated docs: reference-docs/api-docs/django-backend/trips.md, reference-docs/api-docs/django-backend/members.md

docs.title: #2 — Trailing-slash inconsistency across endpoints
docs.text: Priority: Medium Reported: Session #13 (2026-03-30)

docs.title: Problem
docs.text:
Some endpoints require a trailing slash, others return 404 when a slash is present. This causes silent failures when the proxy or client guesses wrong.

Endpoint Without slash With slash Correct form /api/trips 403 (authenticated) 200 With slash /api/levels 301 redirect 200 With slash /api/vehicles 301 redirect 200 With slash /api/choices/carbrand 200 404 Without slash /api/auth/profile/notificationsettings 200 404 Without slash /api/members/request-deletion 200 404 Without slash

docs.title: Recommendation
docs.text:
Standardise all endpoints to accept both forms. Django's APPEND_SLASH setting should handle this, but some endpoints (particularly under /api/choices/ and /api/auth/profile/notificationsettings) appear to bypass it.

The frontend proxy currently works around this with redirect-following and 403/405 retry logic, but a consistent backend would be cleaner.

docs.title: Frontend Audit Notes (from backend docs review — 2026-03-30)
docs.text: Confirmed still needed. Cross-referencing all backend docs reveals: - Endpoints WITH trailing slash (documented): /api/vehicles/, /api/vehicles/{id}/, /api/notifications/mark-as-read/, /api/feedback/, /api/meetingpoints/, /api/trips/, /api/members/. - Endpoints WITHOUT trailing slash (documented): /api/members/request-deletion, /api/auth/profile/notificationsettings. - Live-tested: notifications.md documents the mark-as-read body field as notificationIds (camelCase). Both notificationIds and notification_ids work (both return 204). The error message says notification_ids, so that's the canonical internal name. Both docs are technically correct. - Live-tested: vehicles.md references GET /api/choices/carbrands/ (plural, with slash) — THIS IS WRONG IN THE BACKEND DOCS. Only GET /api/choices/carbrand (singular, no slash) returns 200. All other variants (carbrands/, carbrands, carbrand/) return 404. Backend team must fix vehicles.md. - The trailing-slash inconsistency table in our Problem section is still accurate, and /api/choices/carbrand is another example.

docs.title: Implementation Record
docs.text:
Status: ❌ Won't fix (confirmed by backend team 2026-04-01)

Resolution: The backend team confirmed this is by design: - Router-registered ViewSets (list/detail) — trailing slash required - Manual URL paths (search, choices, profile sub-endpoints) — no trailing slash

The pattern is consistent within each category. The proxy's redirect-follow + 403/405-retry mechanism (Lesson #23/#24) handles this transparently.

Notes for frontend: - Continue using the proxy's two-layer defence (redirect-follow + 405-retry) - Hook URLs should omit trailing slashes — the proxy handles it - See reference-docs/api-docs/django-backend/api-concepts.md for the updated trailing-slash table

docs.title: #3 — Members endpoint: server-side ordering is silently ignored
docs.text: Priority: High Endpoint: GET /api/members/ Reported: Session #14 (2026-03-30)

docs.title: Problem
docs.text:
The GET /api/members/ list endpoint silently ignores the ordering query parameter. All of the following return identical results:

GET /api/members/?ordering=username&pageSize=5
GET /api/members/?ordering=-username&pageSize=5
GET /api/members/?ordering=trip_count&pageSize=5
GET /api/members/?ordering=-trip_count&pageSize=5
GET /api/members/?ordering=tripCount&pageSize=5
GET /api/members/?ordering=first_name&pageSize=5

Tested 2026-03-30: All six calls return the same 5 members in the same order (Admin, MegaMoe, khaiwi, iguana, Neo). Changing the page number confirms the overall order is fixed across pages.

docs.title: Impact
docs.text: The admin members table cannot offer column sorting (by username, name, level, trips, email, paid status). Admins managing 10,610+ members have no way to find the most active members, newest members, or sort alphabetically without using the search endpoint.

docs.title: Recommended fix
docs.text:
Add OrderingFilter to the members viewset. Minimum sortable fields:

ordering_fields = ['username', 'first_name', 'last_name', 'trip_count', 'level__numeric_level', 'date_joined', 'id']

Both ascending (ordering=username) and descending (ordering=-username) should work.

docs.title: Frontend Audit Notes (from backend docs review — 2026-03-30)
docs.text: Confirmed still needed. members.md documents these filter parameters for GET /api/members/: car_brand, car_year, trip_count, phone, level__numeric_level, level__name, email, first_name, last_name, nationality, city — and pagination (page, page_size). No ordering parameter is documented. The backend genuinely has no OrderingFilter configured. - Note on parameter naming: The documented filter params use Django double-underscore syntax (e.g., level__numeric_level) and snake_case. The ordering param should follow the same convention.

docs.text:
Status: ✅ Complete

What was changed: - Added OrderingFilter and SearchFilter to filter_backends in MemberViewSet (api/views/views_member.py) - Added ordering_fields list with 8 sortable fields - Added ordering = ['id'] as default (preserves existing behavior) - Also added DjangoFilterBackend explicitly to filter_backends (was previously implicit via filterset_class)

New/updated endpoint syntax:

Parameter Type Accepted values Default Notes ordering string username, -username, first_name, -first_name, last_name, -last_name, trip_count, -trip_count, level__numeric_level, -level__numeric_level, date_joined, -date_joined, id, -id, last_visited, -last_visited id Prefix with - for descending. Multi-field supported: ordering=-trip_count,username

Example request & response:

curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" \
  "https://ap.ad4x4.com/api/members/?ordering=-trip_count&pageSize=3"
→ { "count": 10610, "results": [{ "username": "khaiwi", "tripCount": 154 }, ...] }

  "https://ap.ad4x4.com/api/members/?ordering=username&pageSize=3"

Breaking changes: None. Default ordering remains id ascending (same as before).

Notes for frontend: - Param name is ordering (Django REST Framework standard) - Field names use snake_case with double underscores for relations (e.g., level__numeric_level). CamelCase field names (e.g., tripCount) do NOT work for ordering — use trip_count. - Invalid field names are silently ignored (falls back to default ordering). No 400 error. - Multi-field ordering is supported: ordering=-trip_count,username - See updated docs: docs/members.md

docs.title: #4 — ~~Members endpoint: level_NumericLevel filter returns 0 results~~ ❌ CLOSED — Not a bug
docs.text: Priority: ~~Medium~~ → Closed Endpoint: GET /api/members/ Reported: Session #14 (2026-03-30) Resolved: Session #14 (2026-03-30) — Frontend misunderstanding, not a backend bug

docs.title: Problem
docs.text:
The API documentation lists level_NumericLevel as a supported integer filter, but it returns 0 results for every value:

GET /api/members/?level_NumericLevel=9&pageSize=1   -> count: 0  (expected: 13 Board members)
GET /api/members/?level_NumericLevel=1&pageSize=1   -> count: 0

Workarounds that DO work:

Filter Example Result level_Name (exact string) ?level_Name=Board%20member 13 results level_Name_Icontains ?level_Name_Icontains=board 13 results level_NumericLevel_Range ?level_NumericLevel_Range=600,900 113 results

docs.title: Frontend Audit Notes (from backend docs review — 2026-03-30)
docs.text:
✅ RESOLVED — NOT A BACKEND BUG. This is a frontend misunderstanding.

Live-tested 2026-03-30 with all numericLevel values:

numericLevel level_NumericLevel= level__numeric_level= Result 5 (Club Event) 0 0 Correct — no members at this level 10 (Newbie+ANIT) 9,247 9,247 ✅ Works 100 (Intermediate) 650 650 ✅ Works 200 (Advanced) 526 526 ✅ Works 300 (Expert) 0 0 Correct — disabled level 400 (Explorer) 74 74 ✅ Works 600 (Marshal) 100 100 ✅ Works 800 (Board member) 13 13 ✅ Works

Priority downgraded: ❌ Not a bug — can be closed.

docs.text:

All valid numericLevel values (5, 10, 100, 200, 300, 400, 600, 800) return correct counts. Both level_NumericLevel and level__numeric_level naming conventions work identically.

docs.title: #6 — Unified advanced search for the members admin panel
docs.text: Priority: High Endpoint: GET /api/members/search and GET /api/members/ Reported: Session #14 (2026-03-30)

docs.title: Problem
docs.text:
The frontend admin panel currently needs to use two different endpoints with different capabilities:

Capability /api/members/ (list) /api/members/search (search) Browse all members Yes No (query is mandatory, min 3 chars) Text search (username, name) No (silently ignored) Yes Filter by level name Yes (level_Name) No Filter by level ID No Yes (level) Filter by min/max level No Yes (minLevel, maxLevel) Server-side ordering No (silently ignored) Not tested Filter by paid status No (silently ignored) Not tested

This forces complex frontend logic to switch between endpoints depending on whether the user has typed a search query or not, using different parameter names for the same concept (level filtering).

docs.title: Recommended enhancement — unified search and filter
docs.text:
Ideally, a single endpoint should handle all admin member queries. Two options:

Option A (preferred): Enhance GET /api/members/ to support text search

Add a search or q parameter to the list endpoint that searches across username, firstname, and lastname (case-insensitive partial match). Combined with the existing level_Name filter and new ordering support, this would cover all admin needs:

GET /api/members/?q=hani&level_Name=Marshal&ordering=-trip_count&paidMember=true&pageSize=20

Option B: Make query optional on GET /api/members/search

Allow the search endpoint to return all members when query is omitted, while retaining its level, minLevel, maxLevel filters. Add ordering support.

docs.text: Field Filter Sort Notes Username Text search (partial, case-insensitive) Ascending/descending First name Text search (partial, case-insensitive) Ascending/descending Last name Text search (partial, case-insensitive) Ascending/descending Level Exact name or ID By numeric level Trip count Range filter Ascending/descending Useful to find most/least active Paid status Boolean exact Currently silently ignored Date joined Range filter Ascending/descending Newest/oldest members Last visited Range filter Ascending/descending See #7 — requires new field Email Text search City Exact or partial match Nationality Exact match Already works

Add clickable column headers for server-side sorting 3. Add paid status filter to the filter bar 4. Add date range filter for "joined date" 5. Add "Last Seen" column, activity indicators, and activity period filter (see #7) 6. Simplify the MembersParams interface to a single set of params

docs.title: #7 — Track and expose "Last Visited" date for members
docs.text: Priority: High Endpoints affected: Member model, GET /api/members/, GET /api/members/search, GET /api/members/{id}/ Reported: Session #14 (2026-03-30)

docs.title: Problem
docs.text: There is currently no record of when a member last accessed the app or website. The admin panel has no way to identify inactive members, measure engagement, or distinguish members who signed up and never returned from regularly active ones.

docs.title: 1. Record the timestamp
docs.text:
Add a last_visited (or last_activity) DateTimeField to the member/profile model. Update it automatically on each authenticated request or on login. Recommended approaches:

  • Option A (lightweight): Update last_visited in the JWT token-obtain view (POST /api/token/). Only records logins, not ongoing activity. Simple but coarse.
  • Option B (recommended): Use Django middleware that updates last_visited on every authenticated request, throttled to once per hour (or configurable interval) to avoid a database write on every single API call. This captures actual usage, not just logins.
# Example middleware (throttled to 1 update per hour)
class LastVisitedMiddleware:
    def __call__(self, request):
        response = self.get_response(request)
        if request.user.is_authenticated:
            now = timezone.now()
            if not request.user.last_visited or (now - request.user.last_visited).seconds > 3600:
                type(request.user).objects.filter(pk=request.user.pk).update(last_visited=now)
        return response

For existing members who have never triggered this middleware, last_visited should default to null (unknown). The admin panel will display "Never" for these.

docs.title: 2. Include in API responses
docs.text:
Add lastVisited (camelCase, matching existing API conventions) to these response schemas:

Endpoint Current fields Add GET /api/members/ id, username, firstName, lastName, phone, level, tripCount, email, paidMember lastVisited (ISO 8601 datetime or null) GET /api/members/search id, username, firstName, lastName, phone, level, tripCount, email, paidMember lastVisited (ISO 8601 datetime or null) GET /api/members/{id}/ (full profile detail) lastVisited (ISO 8601 datetime or null)

docs.title: 3. Support filtering by date range
docs.text:
Add filter support so admins can query members by activity period:

GET /api/members/?lastVisited_Range=2026-01-01,2026-03-30     -> members active in Q1 2026
GET /api/members/?lastVisited_Gte=2026-03-01                  -> members active in last 30 days
GET /api/members/?lastVisited_Lte=2025-12-31                  -> members inactive for 90+ days
GET /api/members/?lastVisited_Isnull=true                     -> members who have NEVER visited

docs.title: 4. Support sorting
docs.text:
GET /api/members/?ordering=-last_visited    -> most recently active first
GET /api/members/?ordering=last_visited     -> longest-inactive first (useful for cleanup)

docs.title: Frontend features this enables
docs.text:
Once lastVisited is available, the admin panel will add:

  1. "Last Seen" column in the members table — displays relative time (e.g., "2 hours ago", "3 months ago", "Never").

  2. Activity status indicator — color-coded dot in each row:

  3. Green: active in the last 7 days
  4. Yellow: last seen 8-30 days ago
  5. Orange: last seen 31-90 days ago

  6. Grey: inactive 90+ days or never visited

  7. Activity period filter — dropdown or date picker in the filter bar:

  8. "Active last 7 days"
  9. "Active last 30 days"
  10. "Inactive 30+ days"
  11. "Inactive 90+ days"
  12. "Never visited"

  13. Custom date range

  14. Admin dashboard widget — "Active Members (last 30 days)" KPI card alongside existing stats (total members, trips, etc.). Helps the board measure engagement at a glance.

  15. Inactive member identification — combined with dateJoined, admins can spot members who signed up but never returned (joined > 30 days ago + lastVisited is null), or members who were once active but dropped off (lastVisited > 90 days ago + tripCount > 0).

  16. Sortable "Last Seen" column — once #3 (ordering support) is also implemented, clicking the column header sorts by most recently active or longest inactive.

docs.title: Data migration note
docs.text: When adding the last_visited field: - Default value: null (not now()) — existing members should show as "Unknown/Never" until they next authenticate - The field should be nullable: last_visited = models.DateTimeField(null=True, blank=True) - No backfill is needed — the field will populate organically as members log in

docs.title: Frontend Audit Notes (from backend docs review — 2026-03-30)
docs.text:
Partially addressed — lastUserActivity already exists but is insufficient.

Live API discovery (2026-03-30): The notification settings endpoint already returns a lastUserActivity field: GET /api/auth/profile/notificationsettings → { "lastUserActivity": "2026-03-31", "member": 10613, ... }

However, this is NOT sufficient for our needs because: 1. ❌ It returns a date ("2026-03-31"), not a datetime — no time precision. 2. ❌ It is only accessible per-user via the notification settings endpoint. An admin cannot query ALL members' last activity in one call. 3. ❌ It is NOT included in GET /api/members/ or GET /api/members/{id}/ responses. 4. ❌ It is NOT filterable — there's no way to query "members active in last 30 days" from the members endpoint. 5. ❌ It is NOT orderable — cannot sort members by last activity.

What this means for implementation: The backend already has the underlying tracking mechanism (the lastUserActivity field updates daily). The work needed is: - Expose this field (or a more precise datetime variant) in member list/detail serializers - Add it to the filterset (with _Gte, _Lte, _Range, _Isnull lookups) - Add it to the ordering fields

This is less work than creating tracking from scratch. The middleware or token-obtain hook is already in place. The remaining work is serializer and filter configuration only. - This is entirely new work — model change, migration, middleware, serializer update, filter configuration. - All assumptions in our Problem section are valid.

docs.title: Implementation Record
docs.text:
Status: ✅ Complete

What was changed: - Added last_visited = models.DateTimeField(null=True, blank=True) to Member model (api/models/models_member.py) - Added database index on last_visited - Created migration 0096_member_last_visited.py - Added LastVisitedMiddleware to api/middleware.py — updates last_visited on authenticated requests, throttled to once per hour - Registered middleware in ad4x4/settings.py - Added last_visited to BasicMemberSerializer fields (api/serializers/serializers_member_base.py) - Added last_visited to ProfileSerializer fields (api/serializers/serializers_member.py) as read-only - Added last_visited as DateTimeFromToRangeFilter + isnull filter to MembersFilter (api/filters.py) - Added last_visited to MemberViewSet.ordering_fields

Which approach was used to record the timestamp? Option B (middleware). The LastVisitedMiddleware runs on every authenticated request but only updates the database if the last update was more than 1 hour ago. Uses .update() (not .save()) to avoid triggering model signals.

New field details: - Model field: last_visited (DateTimeField, nullable, blank, no default — starts as null) - Serializer field: lastVisited (camelCase via CamelCase middleware) - Read-only: Yes — not settable via PATCH

New/updated endpoint syntax:

Parameter Type Example Description last_visited__isnull boolean ?last_visited__isnull=true true = never visited, false = visited at least once last_visited_after datetime ?last_visited_after=2026-03-01 Members active since this date last_visited_before datetime ?last_visited_before=2025-12-31 Members inactive since this date ordering=last_visited string ?ordering=-last_visited Sort by last activity (desc = most recent first)

Example request & response:

  "https://ap.ad4x4.com/api/members/?ordering=-last_visited&pageSize=2"
→ { "count": 10610, "results": [
      { "id": 21144, "username": "elle", "lastVisited": "2026-04-02T14:22:00Z", ... },
      { "id": 10554, "username": "Admin", "lastVisited": null, ... }
    ]}

curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" \
  "https://ap.ad4x4.com/api/members/?last_visited__isnull=true&pageSize=1"
→ { "count": ???, "results": [{ "username": "...", "lastVisited": null, ... }] }

# Members active in last 30 days
