  "https://ap.ad4x4.com/api/members/?last_visited_after=2026-03-03"
→ { "count": ???, "results": [...] }

Breaking changes: None. The lastVisited field is additive in all member list and detail responses. All existing fields are unchanged.

Notes for frontend: - Response field name: lastVisited (camelCase). ISO 8601 datetime with timezone (e.g., "2026-03-30T14:22:00Z"). Nullable — returns null for never-visited members. - Filter param names: last_visited__isnull, last_visited_after, last_visited_before (snake_case with double underscores) - Ordering param: ordering=last_visited or ordering=-last_visited - Update frequency: At most once per hour per user (throttled middleware). Updates on any authenticated API request, not just login. - Initial state: All existing members have lastVisited: null until they next make an authenticated request. No backfill. - Read-only: Cannot be set via PATCH — only updated automatically by the middleware. - Not included in /api/auth/profile/ — only in /api/members/ list and /api/members/{id}/ detail responses. - Migration required: Run python manage.py migrate after deployment. - See updated docs: docs/members.md

docs.title: #8 — Trip search endpoint: approvalStatus, ordering, and meetingPoint (by ID) are silently ignored
docs.text: Priority: High Endpoint: GET /api/trips/search Reported: Session #14 (2026-03-30)

docs.title: Problem
docs.text: The trip search endpoint (GET /api/trips/search) silently ignores three important query parameters. The frontend must fall back to the list endpoint (GET /api/trips/) for these features, requiring complex dual-endpoint switching logic (same pattern as members — see #6).

docs.title: Verified test results (2026-03-30, with JWT auth)
approvalStatus — silently ignored
docs.text:
GET /api/trips/search?query=sand&approvalStatus=A   -> count: 71 (results contain both A and C statuses)
GET /api/trips/search?query=sand&approvalStatus=P   -> count: 71 (identical)
GET /api/trips/search?query=sand&approvalStatus=C   -> count: 71 (identical)
GET /api/trips/search?query=sand                    -> count: 71 (identical — filter has no effect)

docs.title: order — silently ignored
docs.text:
GET /api/trips/search?query=sweihan&order=start_time_asc   -> first result: 2026-12-03
GET /api/trips/search?query=sweihan&order=start_time_desc  -> first result: 2026-12-03 (identical)
GET /api/trips/search?query=sweihan                        -> first result: 2026-12-03 (identical)

All three return the same 466 results in the same order. The order parameter has no effect.

docs.title: meetingPoint (by ID) — silently ignored or broken
docs.text:
GET /api/trips/search?query=sweihan&meetingPoint=117  -> count: 0 (expected: non-zero, as 475 trips use meetingPoint=117 on the list endpoint)
GET /api/trips/search?query=sweihan                   -> count: 466 (without filter)

docs.title: What DOES work on the search endpoint
docs.text: Parameter Status Example query (text search) ✅ Works ?query=sand → 71 results level (numericLevel, not DB id) ✅ Works ?query=sand&level=100 → 15 (Intermediate only) minLevel / maxLevel ✅ Works ?query=sand&minLevel=100 → 40 results area (area code) ✅ Works ?query=sand&area=DXB → 8 results startDateMin / startDateMax ✅ Works ?query=sand&startDateMin=2025-01-01&startDateMax=2025-12-31 → 38 results page / pageSize ✅ Works Standard pagination

docs.title: Comparison with list endpoint (which works correctly)
docs.text: Feature /api/trips/ /api/trips/search approvalStatus ✅ A/P/R/C all work ❌ Silently ignored ordering ✅ -start_time / start_time both work ❌ Silently ignored meetingPoint (by ID) ✅ meetingPoint=142 → 195 results ❌ Returns 0 meetingPoint_Area / area ✅ meetingPoint_Area=DXB → 204 ✅ area=DXB → filters correctly Text search ❌ Not supported ✅ query= works

docs.title: Recommended fix
docs.text:
Add support for these parameters on the search endpoint:

  1. approvalStatus — filter by approval status (P/A/R/C), same as the list endpoint
  2. order or ordering — sort by start_time ascending/descending (confirmed working on list endpoint with ordering)
  3. meetingPoint — filter by meeting point ID (confirmed working on list endpoint)

docs.title: Frontend impact
docs.text:
Currently, the admin trips table hides the status tabs (All/Approved/Pending/Cancelled) when in search mode because the search endpoint ignores approvalStatus. Once fixed, the tabs will work in both browse and search modes.

The sort toggle (Newest/Oldest first) is also disabled in search mode. Once ordering is supported, it will be re-enabled.

docs.title: Frontend Audit Notes (from backend docs review — 2026-03-30)
docs.text: Confirmed still needed, with one correction. - trip-search.md documents these params: query (required, ≥3 chars), level, min_level, max_level, start_date_min, start_date_max, end_date_min, end_date_max, meeting_point, area, page, page_size. No approvalStatus or ordering documented. - ⚠️ Correction on meetingPoint: The backend docs say meeting_point is a text filter (name/keyword match), NOT an ID filter. Our TODO tested meetingPoint=117 (an integer ID) which correctly returned 0. The search endpoint expects a meeting point name string (e.g., meeting_point=Sweihan), not an ID. We should re-test with a name string. If it works with names, the issue is just that ID-based filtering is unsupported (not that the filter is broken). - approvalStatus is genuinely missing — search results include ALL statuses (A, P, C, R). - ordering / order is genuinely missing — results always return in the same default order. - Additional finding: The search endpoint's level param uses numericLevel values (see #10), while the list endpoint uses level_Id. Both approaches should be supported.

docs.title: Implementation Record
docs.text:
Status: ✅ Complete

What was changed: - Added approval_status, level_id, and ordering query parameter support to TripSearch view in api/views/views_trip.py - approval_status validates against {P, A, R, C} and returns 400 for invalid values - level_id filters by database ID (complements existing level param which uses numericLevel) - ordering supports start_time, -start_time, title, -title with fallback to -start_time

New/updated endpoint syntax:

Complete parameter list for GET /api/trips/search after changes:

Parameter Type Required Accepted values Description query string No min 3 chars if provided Text search on trip title. At least one search parameter must be provided. approval_status string No P, A, R, C Filter by approval status. Invalid values return 400. NEW ordering string No start_time, -start_time, title, -title Sort order. Default: -start_time. Invalid values fall back to default. NEW level_id integer No database level ID (1–9) Filter by level database ID. NEW level integer No numericLevel value (5,10,100,...) Filter by numeric level (existing, unchanged) min_level integer No numericLevel value Minimum level (inclusive, existing) max_level integer No numericLevel value Maximum level (inclusive, existing) meeting_point integer No meeting point ID Filter by meeting point ID (existing, already works) area string No area code (AUH, DXB, etc.) Filter by area (existing) start_date_min date No YYYY-MM-DD Trips starting from this date (existing) start_date_max date No YYYY-MM-DD Trips starting until this date (existing) end_date_min date No YYYY-MM-DD Trips ending from this date (existing) end_date_max date No YYYY-MM-DD Trips ending until this date (existing) page integer No ≥1 Page number (default: 1) page_size integer No 1–500 Results per page (default: 20)

Example request & response:

# 1. approval_status — only approved trips
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" \
  "https://ap.ad4x4.com/api/trips/search?query=sand&approval_status=A"
→ { "count": ??? (< 71), "results": [{ "approvalStatus": "A", ... }] }

# 2. ordering — oldest first
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" \
  "https://ap.ad4x4.com/api/trips/search?query=sweihan&ordering=start_time"
→ { "count": 466, "results": [{ "title": "...", "startTime": "2018-...", ... }] }

# 3. ordering — newest first (default)
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" \
  "https://ap.ad4x4.com/api/trips/search?query=sweihan&ordering=-start_time"
→ { "count": 466, "results": [{ "title": "...", "startTime": "2026-...", ... }] }

# 4. level_id — Intermediate only (db id=4)
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" \
  "https://ap.ad4x4.com/api/trips/search?query=sand&level_id=4"
→ { "count": 15, "results": [...] }

# 5. All combined
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" \
  "https://ap.ad4x4.com/api/trips/search?query=sand&approval_status=A&ordering=start_time&level_id=4"

Breaking changes: None. All new params are optional. Default ordering remains -start_time (unchanged). query is still not mandatory (at least one search param required).

Notes for frontend: - Ordering param name: ordering (NOT order). Matches the list endpoint convention. - Valid ordering values: start_time, -start_time, title, -title. Invalid values silently fall back to -start_time. - approval_status values: P (Pending), A (Approved), R (Rejected), C (Cancelled). Invalid → 400 error. - level_id vs level: Both work. level = numericLevel values. level_id = database ID. Use whichever is convenient. - meeting_point already works by ID — the original report of it returning 0 was because combining with query=sweihan narrowed results. The filter itself is functional. Note: the query parameter name is meeting_point (snake_case), not meetingPoint (camelCase). Using meetingPoint will be silently ignored and return unfiltered results. - All params are combinable with each other and with all existing params. - The admin trips table can now enable status tabs and sort toggles in search mode. - See updated docs: docs/trip-search.md

docs.title: #9 — Meeting points: 81% of records have empty area field
docs.text: Priority: Medium Endpoint: GET /api/meetingpoints/ Reported: Session #14 (2026-03-30)

docs.title: Problem
docs.text:
Of 108 total meeting points, 87 (81%) have an empty area field. Only 21 have an area assigned:

Area Count DXB 3 AUH 10 AAN 7 LIW 1 (empty) 87

This means area-based filtering on the trips endpoints (meetingPoint_Area=DXB or area=DXB) only matches trips using the 21 meeting points that have an area assigned. Trips using the other 87 meeting points are invisible to area filters.

docs.title: Recommendation
docs.text:
1. Backfill the area field for existing meeting points based on their names/locations (e.g., "Al Khazna - Sweihan Entrance" → AUH, "Al Madam" → NOR)
  2. Make area required when creating new meeting points to prevent future data gaps
  3. Consider adding a "NOR" (Northern Emirates) area if not already supported — some meeting points may fall into this category

docs.title: Frontend Audit Notes (from backend docs review — 2026-03-30)
docs.text: Confirmed still needed, with one correction. - meeting-points.md documents allowed area values as: DXB, NOR, AUH, AAN, LIW. NOR already exists as a valid area code. Our TODO says "consider adding NOR" — it's already supported. - The area field is NOT marked as required in the POST endpoint docs. Our recommendation to make it required is valid. - HERE Maps integration exists (global-settings.md, here-maps.md): The backend has reverse geocoding via HERE Maps that returns district/city/county info. This could potentially automate the area backfill based on lat/lon coordinates of each meeting point. - The 81% empty area stat should be re-verified — it may have changed if any meeting points were updated since our initial count.

docs.title: Implementation Record
docs.text:
Status: ❌ Deferred — areas will be filled manually

Resolution: The area field will be populated manually by users and admins when the app is operational. The field already exists on the MeetingPoint model and is writable via PATCH /api/meetingpoints/{id}/. No automated backfill.

Rationale: - Many meeting point names don't clearly indicate which emirate they belong to — automated assignment would be error-prone - Admin users with local knowledge are best positioned to assign correct areas - The area field remains optional to avoid blocking meeting point creation

No code changes, no migration, no breaking changes.

Notes for frontend: - The area filter (meetingPoint_Area, area) will only match trips using meeting points that already have an area assigned - Consider adding a UI prompt or admin tool to encourage area assignment when editing meeting points - Valid area codes (already supported): DXB, AUH, AAN, LIW, NOR

docs.title: #10 — Trip search endpoint: level param uses numericLevel not database ID
docs.text: Priority: Low (informational — not a bug, but a documentation/consistency note) Endpoint: GET /api/trips/search Reported: Session #14 (2026-03-30)

docs.title: Observation
docs.text:
The level parameter on the search endpoint uses the numericLevel value, NOT the database id:

GET /api/trips/search?query=sand&level=3     -> count: 0 (id=3 is Newbie, numericLevel=10)
GET /api/trips/search?query=sand&level=100   -> count: 15 (numericLevel=100 = Intermediate) ✅
GET /api/trips/search?query=sand&level=200   -> count: 25 (numericLevel=200 = Advanced) ✅

Meanwhile, the list endpoint uses the database ID:

GET /api/trips/?level_Id=4   -> Intermediate trips (id=4, numericLevel=100) ✅

This inconsistency requires the frontend to maintain a mapping table and translate between ID and numericLevel depending on which endpoint is being called.

docs.title: Current level mapping
docs.text: DB ID numericLevel Name 1 5 Club Event 2 10 ANIT 3 10 Newbie 4 100 Intermediate 5 200 Advanced 6 300 Expert 7 400 Explorer 8 600 Marshal 9 800 Board member

docs.title: Recommendation
docs.text: Either document this clearly, or (preferably) add support for level_Id on the search endpoint as well, matching the list endpoint's parameter name.

docs.title: Frontend Audit Notes (from backend docs review — 2026-03-30)
docs.text: Confirmed, low priority. trip-search.md confirms level param uses numericLevel values. trips.md confirms list endpoint uses level_Id (database ID). - Additional finding from permissions.md: ANIT (numericLevel=10) and Newbie (numericLevel=10) share the same numericLevel value. This means level=10 on the search endpoint matches BOTH Newbie and ANIT trips — there is no way to distinguish them by numericLevel alone. Supporting level_Id on the search endpoint would fix this ambiguity (ANIT=id 2, Newbie=id 3). - Our level mapping table is correct.

docs.title: Implementation Record
docs.text:
Status: ✅ Complete (implemented as part of #8)

What was changed: - Added level_id query parameter to the TripSearch view in api/views/views_trip.py - The existing level param (numericLevel) is unchanged

New/updated endpoint syntax:

All level-related parameters on GET /api/trips/search:

Parameter Type Accepted values Description level integer numericLevel values (5, 10, 100, 200, 300, 400, 600, 800) Filter by numericLevel (existing, unchanged) level_id integer database ID (1–9) Filter by level database ID (NEW) min_level integer numericLevel values Minimum level inclusive (existing) max_level integer numericLevel values Maximum level inclusive (existing)

→ { "count": 15, "results": [...] }  # Intermediate (db id=4, numericLevel=100)

# Existing level param still works

  "https://ap.ad4x4.com/api/trips/search?query=sand&level=100"
→ { "count": 15, "results": [...] }  # Same result

Breaking changes: None. The existing level param behavior is unchanged.

Notes for frontend: - The frontend can now use level_id on both the list endpoint (level__id) and the search endpoint (level_id) for consistent level filtering by database ID - The mapping table is no longer needed if using level_id — but level (numericLevel) still works if preferred - level_id resolves the ANIT/Newbie ambiguity: ANIT (id=2) and Newbie (id=3) share numericLevel=10, but have different database IDs - See updated docs: docs/trip-search.md

More items will be added in future sessions.

docs.title: Backend Response to Flutter App Performance Audit
docs.text: Date: 2026-04-01 In response to: FRONTEND_API_PERFORMANCE_AUDIT.md (2026-03-31) From: Backend Team

docs.title: Summary
docs.text:
We reviewed all 12 findings from the Flutter performance audit. We implemented 4 backend changes that directly address your highest-impact findings. The remaining items are frontend-only optimizations or deferred for now.

What changed on the backend: 1. Trip registration responses now include the updated trip object 2. Cache-Control headers added to static/semi-static endpoints 3. Trip list endpoint now supports registered and waitlisted filters 4. Member trip history endpoint returns richer data (8 new fields)

No breaking changes. All changes are additive — existing response fields and behavior are preserved.

docs.title: T1: Trips List + Home Screen = Duplicate Trip Fetches
docs.text:
Status: No backend change needed (as you noted)

This is a frontend caching concern. The backend now returns Cache-Control headers on static endpoints, but the trips endpoint itself remains uncached since it contains user-specific data (isRegistered, isWaitlisted). Your recommendation to share the upcomingTripsProvider cache between screens is the correct approach.

docs.title: T2: Trip Detail Re-fetched on Every Navigation
docs.text:
Status: No backend change (frontend fix recommended)

Removing the ref.invalidate(tripDetailProvider(trip.id)) call before navigation is the correct fix. The autoDispose + staleness check pattern you already use will handle freshness.

docs.title: T3: Trip Actions Trigger Full List Refresh — IMPLEMENTED
docs.text:
Status: Backend change implemented

All registration endpoints now return the updated trip object in the response body:

POST /api/trips/{id}/register    -> {"success": true, "message": "trip_registered", "trip": { ...full trip object... }}
POST /api/trips/{id}/waitlist    -> {"success": true, "message": "trip_waitlisted", "trip": { ...full trip object... }}
POST /api/trips/{id}/unregister  -> {"success": true, "message": "trip_registration_cancelled", "trip": { ...full trip object... }}

The trip field contains the complete trip object (same schema as GET /api/trips/ list response) with up-to-date registeredCount, waitlistCount, isRegistered, isWaitlisted, etc.

What you need to do on the Flutter side: 1. After a successful registration/waitlist/unregister call, read the trip field from the response 2. Update the local trip in your tripsProvider state with this object 3. Remove the _ref.read(tripsProvider.notifier).refresh() call

API docs reference: See docs/trips.md — Registration section for the full response schema.

docs.title: T4: Member Details Screen — 6+ Waterfall API Calls
docs.text:
Status: Not implementing composite endpoint

We evaluated creating a GET /api/members/{id}/summary/ composite endpoint but decided against it for now. The maintenance cost of a composite endpoint that duplicates 9 existing endpoints is not justified at this project's scale.

What you can do instead: - Use Future.wait() (which you already do) to parallelize the 6+ calls - Cache the results with your existing ApiCacheService - Fix the member_details_screen.dart:28 issue where you create a new MainApiRepository() — use ref.read(mainApiRepositoryProvider) instead to share connection pooling and cache

docs.title: L1: getLogbookSkills() Called by 19 Files — PARTIALLY ADDRESSED
docs.text:
Status: Backend Cache-Control header added

GET /api/logbookskills/ now returns Cache-Control: public, max-age=600 (10 minutes). HTTP clients that respect cache headers will skip the request entirely within the TTL window.

What you need to do on the Flutter side: The backend header provides defense-in-depth, but the real fix is making all 19 files use cachedLogbookSkillsProvider (which already exists in logbook_skills_cache_provider.dart) instead of calling repository.getLogbookSkills() directly.

API docs reference: See docs/logbook.md for the endpoint details.

docs.title: L2: getUpgradeEligibility() Fetched Redundantly
docs.text:
Status: No backend change

The upgrade eligibility endpoint serves user-specific data that varies by member, so a Cache-Control: public header is not appropriate. The fix is frontend-only: create a cachedUpgradeEligibilityProvider similar to your existing cachedLogbookSkillsProvider, with a 5-minute TTL via ApiCacheService.

API docs reference: See docs/upgrade-requests.md — Upgrade Eligibility section.

docs.title: L3: Trip Skill Opportunities = 2 API Calls Per Trip Detail View
docs.text:
Status: No backend change

Both getUpgradeEligibility() and getLogbookSkills() return user-level data that doesn't change between trip views. Cache them on the frontend side as recommended in L1 and L2.

docs.title: L4: Timeline Provider — N+1 Trip Detail Fetches

docs.title: API Performance Audit Report
docs.text: Date: 2026-03-31 Scope: Full Flutter app — all API calls, caching, and data flow patterns Focus: Realistic backend changes to reduce API calls and improve performance

docs.title: Executive Summary
docs.text:
After auditing all 331 Dart files across 16 features, I identified 12 high-impact findings that can significantly reduce API calls. The app already has a solid ApiCacheService (TTL-based, stale-while-revalidate), but many screens and providers bypass it entirely or duplicate calls that could be consolidated.

The biggest wins come from: 1. Deduplicating the getLogbookSkills() catalog call — fetched independently by 19 files, often multiple times per session 2. Adding a backend composite/aggregate endpoint for Member Details (currently 6 parallel API calls) 3. Backend-side trip filtering to eliminate client-side re-filtering

docs.title: Finding T1: Trips List + Home Screen = Duplicate Trip Fetches
docs.text:
Files: trips_provider.dart, upcoming_trips_provider.dart Impact: 2 independent API calls for the same data on app launch

The home screen fetches upcoming trips via upcomingTripsProvider (pageSize: 100), and the trips list screen independently fetches via tripsProvider.loadTrips() (pageSize: 50). Both call GET /api/trips/ with nearly identical filters (approved, endTime > now).

Recommendation (Backend): No backend change needed — this is already partially addressed by the shared upcomingTripsProvider. However, the tripsProvider in the trips list screen does NOT reuse this cache. Consider having the trips list screen consume the same cached provider and apply local filters, or add a backend ETag/Last-Modified header so the Dio client can skip re-downloading identical data.

Recommendation (Quick backend win): Add Cache-Control: max-age=120 and ETag headers to GET /api/trips/. Dio can then send If-None-Match and get 304 Not Modified responses (~50 bytes) instead of the full JSON payload. This saves bandwidth even when data hasn't changed.

docs.title: Finding T2: Trip Detail Re-fetched on Every Navigation
docs.text:
File: trips_list_screen.dart:459 Impact: 1 API call every time user taps a trip card

ref.invalidate(tripDetailProvider(trip.id));
context.push('/trips/${trip.id}');

The code explicitly invalidates the cached trip detail before navigating. This means every tap = fresh API call, even if the user just viewed that trip 10 seconds ago.

Recommendation (Backend): Add ETag support to GET /api/trips/{id}/. The app can then always send the request but get a 304 response when nothing changed. This gives freshness guarantees without the full payload cost.

Alternative (Frontend-only): Remove the invalidate() call and let the autoDispose + staleness check handle it. The trip detail provider already uses FutureProvider.autoDispose, so navigating away disposes it and navigating back fetches fresh.

docs.title: Finding T3: Trip Actions Trigger Full List Refresh
docs.text:
File: trips_provider.dart:557-560 Impact: After register/unregister/waitlist, the entire trips list is refetched

await _ref.read(tripsProvider.notifier).refresh(); // re-fetches ALL trips

Every registration action calls refresh() which calls loadTrips() which fetches the full trips list again. This is heavy — up to 50 trips re-downloaded just because the user registered for one.

Recommendation (Backend): Return the updated trip object in the registration/unregistration response body. Currently the POST /api/trips/{id}/register likely returns a simple success message. If it returned the updated trip (with new registeredCount, isRegistered, isFull, etc.), the frontend could update just that one trip in the list without re-fetching everything.

Example response change:

// Current: {"message": "Successfully registered"}
// Proposed: {"message": "Successfully registered", "trip": { ...full trip object... }}

docs.title: Finding T4: Member Details Screen — 6+ Waterfall API Calls
docs.text:
File: member_details_screen.dart:56-82 Impact: 6 independent API calls PER member view, some with waterfalls

_loadMemberData();           // 1. getMemberDetail()
_loadTripHistory(memberId);  // 2. getMemberTripHistory()
_loadTripStatistics(memberId); // 3. getMemberTripCounts() + 4. getLeadTripHistory(pageSize:1) + 5. getLeadTripHistory(pageSize:200) + 6. getMemberTripHistory(checkedIn:false)
_loadUpgradeHistory(memberId); // 7. getMemberUpgradeRequests()
_loadTripRequests(memberId);   // 8. getMemberTripRequests()
_loadMemberFeedback(memberId); // 9. getMemberFeedback()

The statistics section alone does 4 sequential calls: getMemberTripCounts(), then getLeadTripHistory(pageSize:1) for total count, then getLeadTripHistory(pageSize:200) for per-level breakdown, then another getMemberTripHistory(checkedIn:false) for upcoming count.

Recommendation (Backend — HIGH PRIORITY): Create a single composite endpoint: GET /api/members/{id}/summary/ that returns:

{
  "profile": { ...member data... },
  "tripCounts": { "total": 45, "checkedIn": 40, "asLeader": 12, "upcoming": 3 },
  "leaderByLevel": { "1": 5, "2": 4, "3": 3 },
  "recentTrips": [ ...last 10 trips... ],
  "upgradeRequests": [ ...list... ],
  "tripRequests": [ ...list... ],
  "feedback": [ ...list... ]
}

This reduces 9 API calls down to 1. This is a standard pattern (Google calls them "batch endpoints", Facebook uses "Graph API field expansion").

docs.title: Finding L1: getLogbookSkills() Called by 19 Files Independently (CRITICAL)
docs.text:
Impact: The skills catalog (GET /api/logbookskills/) is fetched independently by 19 different files. Each file calls repository.getLogbookSkills(pageSize: 100-500) directly without going through the cache.

Files making independent calls (bypassing cache): - trip_logbook_section_v2.dart — on every trip detail view - sign_off_bottom_sheet.dart — on every sign-off - bulk_sign_off_bottom_sheet.dart — on every bulk sign-off - trip_skill_opportunities_provider.dart — on every trip detail view - member_logbook_screen.dart — on every logbook view - logbook_entry_detail_screen.dart — on every entry detail - timeline_provider.dart — on every timeline view - trip_skill_planning_provider.dart — on every planning view - certificate_provider.dart — on every certificate view - level_certificates_provider.dart — on every level cert view - migration_request_provider.dart — on every migration view - admin_sign_off_skills_screen.dart — on every admin sign-off - admin_create_logbook_entry_screen.dart — on every admin entry creation - logbook_provider.dart (admin) — on every admin logbook view - admin_logbook_data_provider.dart — on every admin data view - logbook_enrichment_service.dart — on enrichment - level_configuration_service.dart — on level config

Only 1 file uses the cache properly: logbook_skills_cache_provider.dart (via cachedLogbookSkillsProvider)

Recommendation (Backend — EASY WIN): Add Cache-Control: public, max-age=600 (10 minutes) to GET /api/logbookskills/. The skills catalog changes only when an admin modifies skill definitions — this is extremely rare. A 10-minute cache-control header would let the HTTP client skip the request entirely.

Recommendation (Frontend): Make all 19 files use cachedLogbookSkillsProvider instead of calling repository.getLogbookSkills() directly. This is a pure frontend fix but the backend cache header provides defense-in-depth.

docs.title: Finding L2: getUpgradeEligibility() Fetched Redundantly
docs.text:
Files: upgrade_progress_provider.dart, trip_skill_opportunities_provider.dart, skills_matrix_v2_screen.dart, certificate_provider.dart, upgrade_certificate_provider.dart, trip_skill_planning_provider_v2.dart, create_upgrade_request_screen.dart Impact: 7 files call this endpoint independently, and the trip skill opportunities provider calls it ON EVERY TRIP DETAIL VIEW

The upgrade eligibility data (GET /api/members/{id}/upgradeeligibility) changes only when a logbook entry is signed off. Yet it's fetched: - When viewing logbook home - When viewing any trip detail (skill opportunities) - When viewing skills matrix - When viewing certificates - When creating upgrade request

Recommendation (Backend): Add Cache-Control: max-age=300 (5 minutes) to this endpoint. The data only changes after a logbook sign-off action, not on every page view.

Recommendation (Frontend): Create a cachedUpgradeEligibilityProvider similar to cachedLogbookSkillsProvider, using ApiCacheService with CacheCategory.logbookProgress and a 5-minute TTL. All 7 consumers would read from this single provider.

docs.title: Finding L3: Trip Skill Opportunities = 2 API Calls Per Trip Detail View
docs.text:
File: trip_skill_opportunities_provider.dart:76-115 Impact: Every trip detail view triggers getUpgradeEligibility() + getLogbookSkills()

final eligibilityResponse = await repository.getUpgradeEligibility(user.id);
final skillsResponse = await repository.getLogbookSkills(pageSize: 200);

Both are user-level data that doesn't change between trip views.

Recommendation (Backend): Merge skill opportunities into the trip detail response. Add an optional ?expand=skillOpportunities parameter to GET /api/trips/{id}/. When present, the backend includes a skillOpportunities field with the user's relevant unmet requirements for that trip's level. This eliminates 2 extra API calls per trip view.

docs.title: Finding L4: Timeline Provider — N+1 Trip Detail Fetches
docs.text:
File: timeline_provider.dart:137-157 Impact: Fetches each trip individually via getTripDetail(id) in parallel — up to 15+ calls

final tripFutures = tripIds.map((id) async {
  final tripResponse = await repository.getTripDetail(id);
  return MapEntry(id, TripBasicInfo.fromJson(tripResponse));
});

While it uses Future.wait (good), it's still N separate HTTP requests. For a user with 15 trips in their timeline, that's 15 concurrent API calls.

Recommendation (Backend): Add a batch trip endpoint: GET /api/trips/batch/?ids=1,2,3,4,5 that returns multiple trips in one response. This is standard practice (Stripe, Slack, and GitHub all offer batch/bulk endpoints).

Alternative: Add expand=trip to GET /api/members/{id}/logbookentries so the backend returns the trip object inline instead of just the trip ID. This eliminates the N+1 entirely.

docs.title: Finding L5: Logbook Progress = 3 Cached API Calls, But Still 3 Separate Calls
docs.text:
File: logbook_progress_provider.dart:36-52 Impact: 3 parallel API calls (cached with 5-min TTL) every time logbook home is visited

final results = await Future.wait([
  cacheService.getOrFetch(...getMemberLogbookSkills...),
  cacheService.getOrFetch(...getMemberLogbookEntries...),
  cacheService.getOrFetch(...getMemberTripCounts...),
]);

Credit: This is well-implemented with caching. But 3 separate HTTP calls could still be 1.

Recommendation (Backend): Create GET /api/members/{id}/logbook-summary/ returning:

{
  "skills": { "results": [...], "count": 45 },
  "entries": { "results": [...], "count": 20 },
  "tripCounts": { "total": 30, "checkedIn": 25 }
}

This collapses 3 calls into 1. With the existing 5-minute cache, this would mean 1 call every 5 minutes instead of 3.

docs.title: Finding C1: No HTTP-Level Caching (ETags/Last-Modified)
docs.text:
File: api_client.dart Impact: Every API call transfers the full response body, even when data hasn't changed

The Dio client has no If-None-Match or If-Modified-Since interceptor. The app-level cache (ApiCacheService) helps, but when TTLs expire, the full payload is always re-downloaded.

Recommendation (Backend): Add ETag and Last-Modified headers to all GET endpoints. Django REST Framework supports this via ConditionalGetMixin or middleware. This is a one-time backend change that benefits every endpoint:

# Django middleware or mixin
from django.utils.cache import patch_cache_control
from django.views.decorators.http import condition

# On DRF ViewSet:
class TripViewSet(viewsets.ModelViewSet):
    @method_decorator(condition(last_modified_func=get_trips_last_modified))
    def list(self, request, *args, **kwargs):
        ...

For the Flutter side, Dio supports 304 responses natively — no code change needed.

docs.title: Finding C2: Notifications Fetched Without Pagination
docs.text:
File: notification_provider.dart:51 Impact: Fetches ALL notifications every time, no pagination or limit

final response = await repository.getNotifications();

No pageSize, no limit. For active users with hundreds of notifications, this transfers a large payload.

Recommendation (Backend): 1. Add pageSize=50 default to the notifications endpoint 2. Add unread_only=true filter — the home badge only needs unread count, not all notification bodies 3. Better yet: Add a lightweight GET /api/notifications/count/ endpoint that returns just {"unread": 5} for the badge. The full list is only needed when the user opens the notifications screen.

docs.title: Finding C3: Admin Wizard Fetches ALL Trips (pageSize: 200 in a loop)
docs.text:
File: admin_wizard_provider.dart:62-67 Impact: Fetches ALL trips in the database, 200 at a time, in a while loop

const int pageSize = 200;
while (hasMorePages) {
  final response = await repository.getTrips(page: currentPage, pageSize: pageSize);
  ...
}

For a club with hundreds of trips, this downloads everything to the client for client-side filtering.

Recommendation (Backend): Move the admin wizard filtering entirely to the backend. The GET /api/trips/ endpoint already supports most of the filters (level_Id, meetingPoint_Area, startTimeAfter/Before, lead, ordering). The wizard should just send the final filter criteria as query params and let the backend return a single page of results. No pagination loop needed.

docs.title: Finding C4: getLogbookSkillReferences() Not Using Shared Cache
docs.text:
File: skills_comparison_provider.dart:39-58 Impact: Skills comparison fetches skill references for 2 members independently, bypassing cache

The cachedMemberSkillReferencesProvider exists in logbook_skills_cache_provider.dart but the comparison provider doesn't use it — it calls repository.getLogbookSkillReferences() directly.

Recommendation (Backend): No backend change needed. Recommendation (Frontend): Use cachedMemberSkillReferencesProvider in the comparison provider.

docs.title: Finding C5: Member Details Creates New Repository Instance
docs.text:
File: member_details_screen.dart:28 Impact: Bypasses the Riverpod-managed repository and cache

final _repository = MainApiRepository(); // creates new instance

This creates a fresh MainApiRepository (and therefore a fresh ApiClient with a fresh Dio instance) instead of using the Riverpod mainApiRepositoryProvider. This means: - No connection pooling with other screens - No shared interceptors state - No shared cache

Recommendation (Backend): No change needed. Recommendation (Frontend): Use ref.read(mainApiRepositoryProvider) instead.

docs.title: SECTION 4: PRIORITY RANKING
docs.text: Priority Finding API Calls Saved Backend Effort 1 L1: Cache-Control on /api/logbookskills/ ~15-20/session Add 1 header 2 T3: Return updated trip in register/unregister response ~3-5/session Modify response serializer 3 T4: GET /api/members/{id}/summary/ composite endpoint 8 calls -> 1 New endpoint, reuses existing querysets 4 L2: Cache-Control on /api/members/{id}/upgradeeligibility ~5-7/session Add 1 header 5 C1: ETag/Last-Modified on all GET endpoints 30-50% bandwidth Django middleware (one-time) 6 L3: ?expand=skillOpportunities on trip detail 2 calls/trip view New serializer field 7 C2: Notification count endpoint 1 call/screen view New lightweight endpoint 8 L5: GET /api/members/{id}/logbook-summary/ 3 -> 1 New composite endpoint 9 T2: ETag on trip detail 1 call/trip tap Part of C1 10 L4: expand=trip on logbook entries N calls -> 0 DRF expand support 11 C3: Backend-side admin wizard filtering Eliminates loop Already mostly supported 12 T1: Share trip cache between home and list 1 call/launch Frontend only

docs.title: SECTION 5: ESTIMATED IMPACT
docs.text:
Current state (typical user session): - App launch: ~8-10 API calls (home screen widgets + trips + notifications) - View trip details: ~4 API calls (trip detail + logbook skills + upgrade eligibility + skill opportunities) - View logbook: ~4 API calls (progress stats + skills catalog + entries + trip counts) - View member profile: ~9 API calls (profile + trips + stats + leader history x2 + upgrades + requests + feedback) - Total for a 15-minute browsing session: ~40-60 API calls

After implementing Priority 1-6: - App launch: ~5-6 API calls (deduplicated, cached) - View trip details: ~1-2 API calls (composite response, cached skills) - View logbook: ~1-2 API calls (composite endpoint, cached) - View member profile: ~1-2 API calls (summary endpoint) - Total for a 15-minute browsing session: ~12-20 API calls

Estimated reduction: 50-70% fewer API calls

docs.title: SECTION 6: WHAT BIG TECH WOULD DO
docs.text:
1. GraphQL or field expansion (Facebook/Meta): Instead of 9 REST calls for member details, one query that specifies exactly which fields/relations to include. Django Graphene or DRF's ?expand= pattern.

  2. ETag + Conditional GET (Google): Every GET response includes an ETag. Subsequent requests include If-None-Match, getting 304 Not Modified (zero body) when nothing changed. Django's ConditionalGetMiddleware does this automatically.

  3. Response includes mutation result (Stripe/Uber): After POST /register, the response includes the updated trip object. No need for a follow-up GET.

  4. Batch/composite endpoints (Google, Slack): GET /api/batch?endpoints=/trips/1,/trips/2,/trips/3 or purpose-built summary endpoints that join related data server-side.

  5. Cache-Control headers (Every CDN-aware service): Static-ish data (skill catalogs, level definitions, sponsors) gets Cache-Control: public, max-age=3600. Semi-static data gets max-age=300. The HTTP layer handles caching — no app code needed.

  6. Push-based invalidation (Firebase/Supabase): Instead of polling or TTL-based cache, the server pushes "trip 123 updated" events. The app already uses Firestore for chat — the same pattern could extend to trip state changes.

docs.title: Backend Enhancement Implementation Plan
docs.text: Date: 2026-04-01 Scope: Address legitimate findings from Flutter and Website team audits Principle: Industry-standard patterns, zero breaking changes

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
After cross-referencing all three frontend audit documents against the actual backend code and current API documentation, we identified 6 actionable items. All documentation issues from the live test audit were already fixed in prior sessions. The items below are code changes only.

Update (2026-04-01): Changes 1–6 have been implemented. See Round 2 below for the next batch of items addressing BACKENDTODO #3, #5, #6, #7, #8, #10. Item #9 (meeting points area backfill) is deferred — areas will be filled manually by users/admins when the app is operational.

docs.title: Change 1: Add registered and waitlisted Filters to Trips Endpoint
docs.text: Priority: HIGH Source: BACKENDTODO #1, Performance Audit T3 File: api/filters.py

docs.title: What
docs.text: Add two custom filter methods to TripsFilter so that GET /api/trips/?registered=true returns only trips where the authenticated user is registered (and similarly for waitlisted=true).

docs.title: How
docs.text:
Add two BooleanFilter fields with custom method= handlers to TripsFilter. Each method will filter using Exists() subqueries against TripRegistration / TripWaitlist, referencing request.user. This is the standard django-filters pattern for request-aware filtering.

# In TripsFilter:
registered = filters.BooleanFilter(method='filter_registered')
waitlisted = filters.BooleanFilter(method='filter_waitlisted')

def filter_registered(self, queryset, name, value):
    user = self.request.user
    if not user or not user.is_authenticated:
        return queryset
    subquery = TripRegistration.objects.filter(trip=OuterRef('pk'), member=user)
    if value:
        return queryset.filter(Exists(subquery))
    return queryset.exclude(Exists(subquery))

def filter_waitlisted(self, queryset, name, value):
    # Same pattern with TripWaitlist

docs.text: None. This is purely additive. Existing requests without the registered/waitlisted params behave identically.

docs.title: Impact
docs.text:
• Website team: Eliminates fetching all 3,305 trips and filtering client-side. Expected load time drop from 17-30s to <1s.

docs.title: Change 2: Enrich Member Trip History Serializer
docs.text: Priority: HIGH Source: BACKENDTODO #1 (Option B) Files: api/serializers/serializers_trip.py, api/views/views_member.py

docs.title: What
docs.text: Add missing fields to MemberTripHistorySerializer so the website team doesn't need N+1 individual trip detail calls. Fields to add: image, meeting_point, registered_count, capacity, is_registered, is_waitlisted, allow_waitlist, approval_status.

docs.title: How
docs.text:
Serializer changes — Extend MemberTripHistorySerializer to include the missing fields. Use the same patterns already established in ListTripSerializer:

class MemberTripHistorySerializer(serializers.ModelSerializer):
    lead = ConciseMemberSerializer()
    level = LevelSerializer()
    meeting_point = MeetingPointSerializer()
    checked_in = serializers.BooleanField(source='member_checked_in')
    registered_count = serializers.IntegerField(read_only=True)
    is_registered = serializers.BooleanField(read_only=True)
    is_waitlisted = serializers.BooleanField(read_only=True)

    class Meta:
        model = Trip
        fields = (
            'id', 'title', 'description', 'start_time', 'end_time',
            'lead', 'level', 'checked_in', 'image', 'meeting_point',
            'registered_count', 'capacity', 'allow_waitlist',
            'approval_status', 'is_registered', 'is_waitlisted',
        )

View changes — Update the MemberTripHistory queryset to annotate registered_count, is_registered, and is_waitlisted using Count() and Exists() subqueries (same pattern already used in the view for member_checked_in). Also add select_related('meeting_point') which is already in the base mixin.

docs.title: Impact

• Website team: Can use GET /api/members/{id}/triphistory as a drop-in replacement for fetching all trips. Response goes from 8 fields to 16 fields. Eliminates N+1 individual trip detail calls (each 3-13s).
  • Flutter app: Gets richer trip history data without extra calls.

    class Meta:

docs.title: Change 4: Return Updated Trip in Registration Responses
docs.text: Priority: MEDIUM Source: Performance Audit T3 Files: api/views/views_trip.py

docs.title: What
docs.text: After a successful register/unregister/waitlist action, include the updated trip object in the response alongside the existing success message. This follows the Stripe/Uber pattern — mutations return the updated resource.

docs.title: How
docs.text:
After each successful registration action, serialize the trip using ListTripSerializer and include it in the response:

# In RegisterForTrip.post(), after successful registration:
trip.refresh_from_db()
trip_data = ListTripSerializer(trip, context={'request': request}).data
return Response({
    'success': True, 
    'message': msg,
    'trip': trip_data
}, status=status.HTTP_200_OK)

Apply the same pattern to CancelTripRegistration and RegisterForTripWaitlist.

Queryset optimization: Before serializing, ensure the trip has proper prefetches:

trip = Trip.objects.select_related('lead', 'level', 'meeting_point') \
    .prefetch_related('tripregistration_set__member', 'tripwaitlist_set__member') \
    .annotate(
        registered_count=Count('tripregistration'),
        waitlist_count=Count('tripwaitlist')
    ).get(pk=trip.pk)

docs.text: Add Cache-Control headers to endpoints that serve rarely-changing data, using Django's built-in @cache_control decorator. This is the standard HTTP caching pattern used by every CDN-aware service.

docs.title: Endpoints and TTLs
docs.text: Endpoint TTL Rationale GET /api/logbookskills/ 10 min (600s) Skills catalog changes only when admin edits definitions GET /api/levels/ 30 min (1800s) Levels almost never change GET /api/meetingpoints/ 10 min (600s) Meeting points rarely change GET /api/sponsors/ 30 min (1800s) Sponsor list changes rarely GET /api/faqs/ 30 min (1800s) FAQ content changes rarely GET /api/choices/carbrand 60 min (3600s) Car brand list is essentially static

docs.title: How
docs.text:
Use Django's @method_decorator(cache_control(...)) on the list action of each ViewSet:

from django.utils.decorators import method_decorator
from django.views.decorators.cache import cache_control

class LogbookSkillViewSet(viewsets.ReadOnlyModelViewSet):
    @method_decorator(cache_control(public=True, max_age=600))
    def list(self, request, *args, **kwargs):
        return super().list(request, *args, **kwargs)

For endpoints that include user-specific data (trips, members), we do NOT add caching headers — those must remain private / no-cache by default.

docs.title: Breaking Changes
docs.text: None. Cache-Control headers are advisory. Clients that don't implement HTTP caching are unaffected. Clients with Dio/OkHttp/Axios will automatically benefit.

docs.title: Impact
docs.text:
• Reduces redundant fetches of static data (logbook skills fetched by 19 Flutter files independently).
  • Saves bandwidth on every cache hit (304 Not Modified or skip entirely).

docs.title: Change 7: Member Ordering (BACKENDTODO #3)
docs.text: Priority: HIGH File: api/views/views_member.py (lines 112–139, MemberViewSet)

docs.title: Problem
docs.text: GET /api/members/?ordering=-trip_count is silently ignored. The admin members table cannot offer column sorting.

docs.title: Current State
docs.text: MemberViewSet uses filterset_class = MembersFilter but has no filter_backends list declared, no OrderingFilter, and no ordering_fields. The queryset is hardcoded to .order_by('id').

docs.title: What to Change
docs.text:
Add DRF's OrderingFilter to the viewset:

from rest_framework import filters as drf_filters
from django_filters.rest_framework import DjangoFilterBackend

class MemberViewSet(...):
    queryset = Member.objects.all().order_by('id')
    filter_backends = [DjangoFilterBackend, drf_filters.OrderingFilter]
    filterset_class = MembersFilter
    ordering_fields = [
        'username', 'first_name', 'last_name',
        'trip_count', 'level__numeric_level',
        'date_joined', 'id'
    ]
    ordering = ['id']  # default — preserves current behavior

docs.title: Result
docs.text:
GET /api/members/?ordering=-trip_count          → most active first
GET /api/members/?ordering=username             → alphabetical
GET /api/members/?ordering=-date_joined         → newest first
GET /api/members/?ordering=level__numeric_level → lowest level first
GET /api/members/?ordering=-trip_count,username  → multi-field supported

docs.title: Breaking Changes
docs.text: None. Default ordering remains id ascending. The ordering param is optional and ignored if not provided.

docs.title: Notes for Frontend
docs.text:
• Param name is ordering (Django REST Framework standard)
  • Prefix with - for descending (e.g., ordering=-trip_count)
  • Invalid field names are silently ignored (returns default ordering)
  • Multi-field ordering supported: ordering=-trip_count,username
  • Field names use snake_case with double underscores for relations (e.g., level__numeric_level)

docs.title: Change 10: Last Visited Tracking (BACKENDTODO #7)
docs.text:
Priority: HIGH Files: 6 files + 1 new migration

This is the most complex item. It has four sub-tasks.

docs.title: Problem
docs.text: There is no record of when a member last accessed the API. Admins cannot identify inactive members or measure engagement. The existing last_user_activity field on NotificationSettings is insufficient (date-only, not in member responses, not filterable).

docs.title: 10a. Add last_visited Field to Member Model
docs.text:
File: api/models/models_member.py (after line 77, token_version)

last_visited = models.DateTimeField(null=True, blank=True)

Add database index (in Meta.indexes):

models.Index(fields=['last_visited']),

Create migration: python manage.py makemigrations api

Default: null — existing members show as "Never" until they next authenticate. No data backfill.

docs.title: 10b. Add LastVisitedMiddleware
docs.text:
File: api/middleware.py (new class, append after MediaCorsMiddleware)

from django.utils import timezone

class LastVisitedMiddleware:
    def __init__(self, get_response):
        self.get_response = get_response

    def __call__(self, request):
        response = self.get_response(request)
        if hasattr(request, 'user') and request.user.is_authenticated:
            now = timezone.now()
            last = request.user.last_visited
            if not last or (now - last).total_seconds() > 3600:
                type(request.user).objects.filter(
                    pk=request.user.pk
                ).update(last_visited=now)
        return response

Register in settings: ad4x4/settings.py, add 'api.middleware.LastVisitedMiddleware' to MIDDLEWARE list after AuthenticationMiddleware.

Design decisions: - Throttle: Updates at most once per hour per user (avoids a DB write on every request) - Uses .update(): Bypasses model .save() to avoid triggering signals or updating other auto-fields - Placed after AuthenticationMiddleware: Ensures request.user is populated

docs.text:
File: api/serializers/serializers_member_base.py (line 36)

Add last_visited to BasicMemberSerializer.Meta.fields:

fields = ('id', 'username', 'first_name', 'last_name', 'phone', 'level',
          'trip_count', 'email', 'paid_member', 'last_visited')

File: api/serializers/serializers_member.py (ProfileSerializer)

Add last_visited to the detail serializer fields as well.

Response field name: lastVisited (camelCase via CamelCase middleware). ISO 8601 datetime with timezone (e.g., "2026-03-30T14:22:00Z"). Nullable — returns null for never-visited members.

    last_visited = DateTimeFromToRangeFilter()   # <-- ADD

GET /api/members/?last_visited_before=2025-12-31      → inactive for 90+ days
GET /api/members/?last_visited__isnull=true            → never visited
GET /api/members/?last_visited__isnull=false           → visited at least once

File: api/views/views_member.py (MemberViewSet)

Add 'last_visited' to ordering_fields (from Change 7):

    'username', 'first_name', 'last_name',
    'trip_count', 'level__numeric_level',
    'date_joined', 'id', 'last_visited'        # <-- ADD
]

This enables:

GET /api/members/?ordering=-last_visited  → most recently active first
GET /api/members/?ordering=last_visited   → longest-inactive first

docs.text:

  • Ordering: ordering=last_visited / ordering=-last_visited

docs.title: Change 11: Trip Search Enhancements (BACKENDTODO #8 + #10)
docs.text: Priority: HIGH File: api/views/views_trip.py (lines 899–978, TripSearch)

docs.title: Problem
docs.text: The trip search endpoint (GET /api/trips/search) silently ignores approvalStatus and ordering. It also lacks level_id support (#10) — the level param uses numericLevel values, while the list endpoint uses level__id.

docs.title: Current State
docs.text: TripSearch is a manually-coded ListAPIView that parses query params and builds a Q() filter. It supports: query, level, min_level, max_level, start_date_min/max, end_date_min/max, meeting_point (by ID), area. Results are always ordered by -start_time, id.

docs.title: What to Change
docs.text: Add three new parameters to the existing manual parsing logic:

docs.title: 11a. approval_status filter
docs.text:
approval_status = request.query_params.get('approval_status', None)
if approval_status is not None:
    if approval_status not in ['P', 'A', 'R', 'C']:
        return Response(
            {'success': False, 'message': 'invalid_approval_status'},
            status=status.HTTP_400_BAD_REQUEST
        )
    filters &= Q(approval_status=approval_status)

docs.title: 11b. ordering support
docs.text:
ordering = request.query_params.get('ordering', '-start_time')
valid_orderings = {'start_time', '-start_time', 'title', '-title'}
if ordering not in valid_orderings:
    ordering = '-start_time'

# Then use in queryset:
queryset = Trip.objects.filter(filters).select_related(...).order_by(ordering, 'id')

docs.title: 11c. level_id filter (resolves #10)
docs.text:
level_id = request.query_params.get('level_id', None)
if level_id is not None:
    try:
        filters &= Q(level__id=int(level_id))
    except ValueError:
        return Response(
            {'success': False, 'message': 'invalid_level_id'},
            status=status.HTTP_400_BAD_REQUEST
        )

docs.title: Result
docs.text:
# Filter by approval status
GET /api/trips/search?query=sand&approval_status=A   → only approved trips

# Sort by date
GET /api/trips/search?query=sweihan&ordering=start_time    → oldest first
GET /api/trips/search?query=sweihan&ordering=-start_time   → newest first (default)

# Filter by level database ID
GET /api/trips/search?query=sand&level_id=4   → only Intermediate trips (db id=4)

# All three combined
GET /api/trips/search?query=sand&approval_status=A&ordering=start_time&level_id=4

docs.title: Meeting Point Filter — Already Works
docs.text: Correction from frontend audit: The meeting_point param on the search endpoint already works by ID (see code lines 955–960). The frontend team's test returned 0 because meeting_point=117 combined with query=sweihan narrowed results to zero. The filter itself is functional. No change needed.

docs.title: Breaking Changes
docs.text: None. All new params are optional. Existing behavior is preserved: - Default ordering remains -start_time, id when no ordering param is provided - The existing level param (numericLevel) continues to work unchanged - level_id is a separate, additive param

docs.title: Notes for Frontend
docs.text:
• approval_status values: P (Pending), A (Approved), R (Rejected), C (Cancelled). Invalid values return 400.
  • ordering param name: ordering (matches the list endpoint convention, NOT order)
  • Valid ordering values: start_time, -start_time, title, -title. Invalid values fall back to -start_time.
  • level_id vs level: Both work. level filters by numericLevel value (5, 10, 100, etc.). level_id filters by database ID (1–9). Use whichever is more convenient.
  • All params combinable: approval_status, ordering, level_id, and level can be combined with each other and with all existing params (query, area, meeting_point, dates).

docs.title: Item #9 — Meeting Points Area Backfill — DEFERRED
docs.text:
Decision: Not implementing. The area field on meeting points will be filled manually by users and admins when the app is operational.

Rationale: - The area field already exists on the MeetingPoint model and is writable via PATCH /api/meetingpoints/{id}/ - Automated backfill based on names would be error-prone — many meeting point names don't clearly indicate which emirate they belong to - Admin users with local knowledge are best positioned to assign correct areas - The area field is not being made required — it stays optional to avoid blocking meeting point creation

No code changes needed.

docs.title: Backend API Documentation Audit
docs.text:
Purpose: This report documents every discrepancy found between the backend API documentation (ad4x4-backend/docs/) and the actual live API behaviour. Each item tells the backend team exactly what to fix in their docs.

Tested by: Frontend AI developer (Session #14) Date: 2026-03-30 API base: https://ap.ad4x4.com Test user: hani amj (ID 10613, Board member, admin permissions) Method: Every endpoint was tested with curl + Bearer JWT token

Scope limitation: All tests were performed with a Board member (admin) account that has full permissions. This means: - Covered: Endpoint URLs, trailing slashes, HTTP methods, response field names/structures, filter parameters, pagination, query validation — all verified. - NOT covered: Permission-gated behaviour. Endpoints that restrict access or hide fields based on user level were not tested with a lower-permission account. Examples: - GET /api/members/ may hide phone/email fields for users without VIEW_CONTACT_INFO permission. - GET /api/members/search requires SEARCH_MEMBERS permission — a Newbie may get 403. - GET /api/upgraderequests/ requires VIEW_UPGRADE_REQ permission. - Trip registration vehicle_required enforcement may differ for staff vs regular users. - Self-only restrictions (e.g., editing own profile vs another member's) not tested. - Recommendation: When building features that use permission-restricted endpoints, test with a regular member account (e.g., Newbie or Intermediate level) to verify the actual permission behaviour.

docs.text:
1. vehicles.md — Wrong endpoint name: says /api/choices/carbrands/, reality is /api/choices/carbrand
  2. auth-profiles.md — Wrong field names for change-password: says old_password, password, password2, reality is oldPassword, password, passwordConfirm
  3. members.md — Documents car_brand and car_year as working filters, but they are silently ignored
  4. logbook.md — Documents endpoint as /api/logbookskills (no slash), but that returns 301; only /api/logbookskills/ (with slash) returns 200
  5. global-settings.md — Documents GET /api/settings/, but endpoint returns 404 (may not be exposed to API)
  6. trip-search.md — Documents meeting_point parameter but doesn't clarify it's a text filter; using an integer ID returns 0 results and a text name causes timeout
  7. members.md — Missing documentation for email filter behaviour (requires exact match or __icontains suffix)
  8. sponsorships.md — Wrong endpoint name: says /api/sponsorships/, reality is /api/sponsors/ (plain array, not paginated)
  9. club-news.md — Wrong response fields: docs say published and author, reality is submitDate (no author field). Actual fields: id, title, content, submitDate, status, levels, image
  10. members.md — level_Id filter is silently ignored on the list endpoint (level_Id=9, level__id=9, levelId=9 all return full count 10,610)
  11. members.md — dateJoined range filters (dateJoined_Gte, date_joined__gte) are silently ignored
  12. lead-trip-history.md — Docs show URL without trip- prefix (just lead-trip-history), but reality confirms the correct URL is /api/trips/lead-trip-history (no trailing slash; slash returns 404)
  13. upgrade-requests.md — Minor: response field names use camelCase (finalApprover, applicantStr, verdictDate) not snake_case as some docs imply
  14. trips.md — Trip approve endpoint: POST /api/trips/{id}/approve works (no slash). With slash → 404. Not documented which HTTP methods are supported.

docs.title: Comprehensive Trailing-Slash Reference
docs.text:
This table captures the slash behaviour for every endpoint tested:

Endpoint Without Slash With Slash Canonical Form /api/members 301 → 200 200 With slash /api/members/{id} 301 → 200 200 With slash /api/members/search 200 404 No slash /api/members/{id}/triphistory 200 404 No slash /api/members/{id}/tripcounts 200 404 No slash /api/members/{id}/logbookentries 200 404 No slash /api/members/{id}/upgradeeligibility 200 404 No slash /api/members/leadsearch 400 (needs query) 404 No slash /api/members/activetripleads 200 404 No slash /api/members/request-deletion 405 (POST only) 404 No slash /api/trips 405 200 With slash /api/trips/{id} 301 → 200 200 With slash /api/trips/search 200 404 No slash /api/trips/{id}/viewlogbooks 200 404 No slash /api/trips/{id}/logbook-entries 405 (POST only) 404 No slash /api/trips/{id}/approve 200 (POST) 404 No slash /api/trips/lead-trip-history 200 404 No slash /api/token 301 → 200 200 With slash /api/token/refresh 301 → 200 200 With slash /api/vehicles 301 → 200 200 With slash /api/meetingpoints 301 → 200 200 With slash /api/notifications 301 → 200 200 With slash /api/notifications/mark-as-read 301 → 204 204 With slash /api/feedback 301 → 405 405 With slash /api/levels 301 → 200 200 With slash /api/device/fcm 301 → 200 200 With slash /api/logbookskills 301 → 200 200 With slash /api/clubnews 301 → 200 200 With slash /api/triprequests 301 → 200 200 With slash /api/upgraderequests 301 → 200 200 With slash /api/tripreports 301 → 200 200 With slash /api/faqs 301 → 200 200 With slash /api/sponsors 301 → 200 200 With slash /api/strings 301 → 200 200 With slash /api/settings 404 404 Broken /api/sponsorships 404 404 Wrong name (use /api/sponsors/) /api/choices/carbrand 200 404 No slash /api/choices/triprequestarea 200 404 No slash /api/auth/profile/notificationsettings 200 404 No slash /api/auth/change-password 301 405 (POST only) With slash

Pattern: Main resource endpoints (members, trips, vehicles, meetingpoints, notifications, levels, logbookskills, token) work WITH trailing slash. Sub-action endpoints (search, triphistory, tripcounts, viewlogbooks, etc.) work WITHOUT trailing slash. /api/choices/* endpoints work WITHOUT slash. This pattern should be documented.

docs.title: Discovery: lastUserActivity Field (relevant to BACKENDTODO #7)
docs.text:
During the audit, we discovered an undocumented field lastUserActivity in the notification settings response:

GET /api/auth/profile/notificationsettings
→ {
    "clubNewsEnabledEmail": true,
    "clubNewsEnabledAppPush": true,
    "newTripAlertsEnabledEmail": true,
    "newTripAlertsEnabledAppPush": true,
    "upgradeRequestReminderEmail": true,
    "tripChatEnabledAppPush": true,
    "lastUserActivity": "2026-03-31",
    "member": 10613,
    "newTripAlertsLevelFilter": []
  }

Key findings: - The lastUserActivity field returns a date (not datetime) — "2026-03-31" format. - It is NOT included in member list or detail responses (GET /api/members/, GET /api/members/{id}/). - It is only accessible via the notification settings endpoint (which is per-user, not admin-queryable). - For BACKENDTODO #7 to work fully, lastUserActivity (or a lastVisited field) needs to be: 1. Added to the member list/detail response 2. Made filterable (for admin queries like "inactive 90+ days") 3. Made orderable (for sorting by last activity)

The existence of this field suggests the backend already tracks user activity at some level, which means implementing #7 may be simpler than creating it from scratch.

End of audit. Updated 2026-03-30 (Session #14 continued).
